muyesser-irab:97-97.t: ﴿تالله إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿تالله﴾ are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "نقسم", and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of ﴿قالوا﴾; ﴿إن﴾ is lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy [إنّ] and inoperative (muhmala); كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); ﴿في ضلال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿كان﴾; and مبين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:98-98.t: ﴿إذ نسويكم برب العالمين﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كنّا في ضلال﴾ in the previous verse, or attached to an omitted verb, the implied form being "ضللنا إذ نسويكم"; ﴿نسويكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, the fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿نسويكم﴾ is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; and ﴿برب العالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نسويكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:99-99.t: ﴿وما أضلنا إلا المجرمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما is negating; أضلنا is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and المجرمون is the fāʿil (agent) of أضلنا.

muyesser-irab:100-100.t: ﴿فما لنا من شافعين﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); ما is negating; ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿من﴾ is a connective (ṣila) particle; and ﴿شافعين﴾ is genitive in form and nominative in position as the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:101-101.t: ﴿ولا صديق حميم﴾: conjoined to شافعين, and حميم is a naʿt (adjective) of صديق.

muyesser-irab:102-102.t: ﴿فلو أن لنا كرة فنكون من المؤمنين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; لو is a particle of wishing (tamannī) or of condition, and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, its implied form being "we would have done such-and-such"; ﴿أن﴾ is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and أن together with what falls in its scope is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "نتمنى", or the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb if ﴿لو﴾ is conditional; ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of أن; ﴿كرة﴾ is the postponed noun of أن; the clause ﴿فلو أن...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿فنكون﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and ﴿نكون﴾ is an imperfect verb made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e. "would that we had a return, and [so] our being among the believers"; the noun of نكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; and ﴿من المؤمنين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of نكون.

muyesser-irab:103-103.t: ﴿إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين﴾: إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿في ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿آية﴾ is its postponed noun; ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, أكثرهم is its noun, and مؤمنين is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:104-104.t: ﴿وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and ربك is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿هو﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), العزيز is the khabar (predicate) of إن and الرحيم a second khabar; or ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), العزيز is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾ and الرحيم a second khabar, and the clause ﴿هو العزيز الرحيم﴾ is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:105-105.t: ﴿كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين﴾: كذبت is a past verb; قوم is the fāʿil (agent) and نوح is muḍāf ilayhi; and المرسلين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:106-106.t: ﴿إذ قال لهم أخوهم نوح ألا تتقون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قال﴾; ﴿أخوهم﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿قال﴾, and نوح is a badal (substitute); ألا is a particle of proposal (ʿarḍ); and تتقون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:107-107.t: ﴿إني لكم رسول أمين﴾: إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to رسول; ﴿رسول﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and أمين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:108-108.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأطيعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:109-109.t: ﴿وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; أسألكم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿أجر﴾ is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is a mafʿūl bihi; إن is negating; أجري is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿على رب العالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:110-110.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأطيعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:111-111.t: ﴿قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون﴾: قال is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿أنؤمن﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and نؤمن is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "نحن"; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نؤمن﴾; the wāw is circumstantial (for ḥāl), with قد implied; ﴿اتبعك الأرذلون﴾: اتبع is a past verb, the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الأرذلون is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:112-112.t: ﴿قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون﴾: قال is a past verb; the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿ما﴾ is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and علمي is its khabar (predicate); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿علمي﴾; or ﴿ما﴾ is negating and the khabar is omitted; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position. The clause يعملون is the khabar of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:113-113.t: ﴿إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون﴾: إن is negating; حسابهم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿على ربي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿حسابهم﴾; لو is of non-occurrence (imtināʿiyya); تشعرون is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb; and the apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being "you would not have found fault with them, nor attributed any deficiency to them".

muyesser-irab:114-114.t: ﴿وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating ما that operates like ليس; ﴿أنا﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بطارد﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿طارد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive in form by the bāʾ; and ﴿المؤمنين﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:115-115.t: ﴿إن أنا إلا نذير مبين﴾: إن is negating; أنا is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); نذير is the khabar (predicate), and مبين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:116-116.t: ﴿قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح لتكونن من المرجومين﴾: قال is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and إن is conditional; ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; تنته is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿لتكونن﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted; تكونن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the noun of تكونن is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; and ﴿من المرجومين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:117-117.t: ﴿قال رب إن قومي كذبون﴾: قال is a past verb; ﴿رب﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, قومي is its noun, and the clause كذبون is its khabar (predicate); كذبون is a past verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the first-person yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:118-118.t: ﴿فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); افتح is a verb of request, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿بيني﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿افتح﴾, and ﴿بينهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿بيني﴾; فتحًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ونجني﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and نجني is conjoined to ﴿افتح﴾; ﴿ومَن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or of accompaniment (maʿiyya), and مَن is conjoined to the yāʾ in ﴿نجني﴾, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); ﴿معي﴾ is an adverb attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of مَن, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿من المؤمنين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:119-119.t: ﴿فأنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك المشحون﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; أنجيناه is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مَن is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), or conjoined to the hāʾ in أنجيناه; ﴿معه﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿في الفلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the [notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār) to which the adverb is attached; and المشحون is a naʿt (adjective) of الفلك.

muyesser-irab:120-120.t: ﴿ثم أغرقنا بعد الباقين﴾: ثم is a conjunction denoting delay (tarākhī); أغرقنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بعد﴾ is an adverb of time indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, the intended sense being "after rescuing them"; and الباقين is the object of أغرقنا.

muyesser-irab:121-121.t: ﴿إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين﴾: إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿في ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آية is the postponed noun of إن; the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, أكثرهم is its noun, and مؤمنين is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:122-122.t: ﴿وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and ربك is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿هو﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), العزيز is the khabar (predicate) of إن and الرحيم a second khabar; or ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), العزيز is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾ and الرحيم a second khabar, and the clause ﴿هو العزيز الرحيم﴾ is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:123-123.t: ﴿كذبت عاد المرسلين﴾: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:124-124.t: ﴿إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قال﴾; أخوهم is the fāʿil (agent), and هود is a badal (substitute) from ﴿أخوهم﴾; ألا is a particle of proposal (ʿarḍ); تتقون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:125-125.t: ﴿إني لكم رسول أمين﴾: the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to رسول; رسول is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and أمين is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول.

muyesser-irab:126-126.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وأطيعون: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:127-127.t: ﴿وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; أسألكم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿أجر﴾ is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is a mafʿūl bihi; إن is negating; أجري is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿على رب العالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:128-128.t: ﴿أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون﴾: the question is for reproach and rebuke; تبنون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بكل ريع﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تبنون﴾; آية is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); تعبثون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause تعبثون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:129-129.t: ﴿وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and تتخذون is conjoined to تبنون; تتخذون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and مصانع is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لعلكم تخلدون﴾: لعل is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, the kāf is its noun, and the clause تخلدون is its khabar (predicate); the clause of hope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "hoping and expecting to be immortal in this world".

muyesser-irab:130-130.t: ﴿وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis, which is the second بطشتم; بطشتم is a past verb and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the first clause بطشتم is in the position of the genitive through ﴿إذا﴾ being annexed to it; and جبارين is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "heedless of results and consequences".

muyesser-irab:131-131.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وأطيعون: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:132-132.t: ﴿واتقوا الذي أمدكم بما تعلمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; اتقوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); الذي is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أمدكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative and has no grammatical position. ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمدكم﴾; and the clause تعلمون is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:133-133.t: ﴿أمدكم بأنعام وبنين﴾: أمدكم: a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent. ﴿بأنعام﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمدكم﴾. بنين: conjoined to ﴿أنعام﴾. The clause ﴿أمدكم بأنعام﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the preceding clause ﴿أمدكم بما تعلمون﴾ and has no grammatical position; or it is a badal (substitute) from the clause ﴿أمدكم بما تعلمون﴾, with the governor repeated.

muyesser-irab:135-135.t: ﴿إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم﴾: إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause أخاف is its khabar (predicate); ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخاف﴾; عذاب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), يوم is muḍāf ilayhi, and عظيم is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:136-136.t: ﴿قالوا سواء علينا أوعظت أم لم تكن من الواعظين﴾: سواء is a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿علينا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سواء﴾; the hamza is interrogative; ﴿وعظت﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); أم is a conjunction; ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; ﴿تكن﴾ is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and its noun is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿من الواعظين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and the hamza of equivalence (taswiya) together with what falls in its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "your admonishing is all the same to us".

muyesser-irab:137-137.t: ﴿إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين﴾: إن is negating; هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); خلق is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هذا﴾, and الأولين is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:138-138.t: ﴿وما نحن بمعذبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating ما that operates like ليس; ﴿نحن﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بمعذبين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿معذبين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive in form by the bāʾ.

muyesser-irab:139-139.t:
﴿فكذبوه فأهلكناهم﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); كذبوه is a past verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فأهلكناهم is conjoined to ﴿فكذبوه﴾.
﴿إن في ذلك لآية﴾: إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿في ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and آية is the noun of إن.
﴿وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, أكثرهم is its noun, and مؤمنين is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:140-140.t: ﴿وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, رب is the noun of إن and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); العزيز is the first khabar (predicate) of إن and الرحيم the second khabar; or ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), العزيز is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾ and الرحيم a second khabar, and the clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:141-141.t: ﴿كذبت ثمود المرسلين﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; كذبت is a past verb, ثمود is the fāʿil (agent), and المرسلين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:142-142.t: ﴿إذ قال لهم أخوهم صالح ألا تتقون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قال﴾; ﴿أخوهم﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and صالح is a badal (substitute) from ﴿أخوهم﴾; ألا is a particle of proposal (ʿarḍ); تتقون is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:143-143.t: ﴿إني لكم رسول أمين﴾: the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to رسول; رسول is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and أمين is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول.

muyesser-irab:144-144.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأطيعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:145-145.t: ﴿وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; ﴿أسألكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿أجر﴾ is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is a mafʿūl bihi; إن is negating; أجري is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿على رب العالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:146-146.t: ﴿أتتركون في ما ههنا آمنين﴾: the hamza is interrogative; تتركون is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿فيما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تتركون﴾; ﴿ها﴾ is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh), and هنا is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position. آمنين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in تتركون.

muyesser-irab:147-147.t: ﴿في جنات وعيون﴾: ﴿في جنات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is a badal (substitute) from His words ﴿فيما هاهنا﴾, with the preposition repeated; and عيون is conjoined to جنات.

muyesser-irab:148-148.t: ﴿وزروع ونخل طلعها هضيم﴾: ﴿زروع ونخل﴾ is conjoined to جنات; طلعها is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and هضيم is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of نخل.

muyesser-irab:149-149.t: ﴿وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا فارهين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; تنحتون is conjoined to تتركون, so it falls within the scope of the question of disapproval and rebuke, and the position of the rebuking interrogative clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿من الجبال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنحتون﴾; بيوتًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and فارهين is a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:150-150.t: ﴿فاتقوا الله وأطيعون﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأطيعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أطيعون is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ — dropped out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil) — is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:151-151.t: ﴿ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تطيعوا is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and أمر المسرفين is an object.

muyesser-irab:152-152.t: ﴿الذين يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of المسرفين; the clause يفسدون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative and has no grammatical position. ﴿في الأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفسدون﴾; and ولا يصلحون is conjoined to His word يفسدون.

muyesser-irab:153-153.t: ﴿قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين﴾: إنما is [إنّ as] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنت is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿من المسحرين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:154-154.t: ﴿ما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا فأت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين﴾: ما is negating; أنت is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); بشر is the khabar (predicate), and مثلنا is a naʿt (adjective); ﴿فائت﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you are truthful as you claim, then bring"; ﴿بآية﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) His word فائت; إن is conditional; ﴿كنت﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and the tāʾ is its noun, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿من الصادقين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of كان; and the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring a sign".

muyesser-irab:155-155.t: ﴿قال هذه ناقة لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم﴾: هذه is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ناقة is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿لها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar, and شرب is the postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of ناقة; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar, and شرب يوم is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and معلوم is a naʿt of يوم.

muyesser-irab:156-156.t: ﴿ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تمسوها is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by لا, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بسوء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تمسوها﴾; ﴿فيأخذكم﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and يأخذكم is an imperfect verb made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no touching, and [so] a seizing"; عذاب is the fāʿil, يوم is muḍāf ilayhi, and عظيم is a naʿt (adjective) of يوم.

muyesser-irab:157-157.t: ﴿فعقروها فأصبحوا نادمين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; عقروها is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فأصبحوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿أصبحوا نادمين﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw is its noun and نادمين is its khabar (predicate); or ﴿أصبحوا﴾ is complete (tāmma), the wāw is the fāʿil, and نادمين is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:158-158.t:
﴿فأخذهم العذاب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذهم is a past verb, the hāʾ is a fronted object, and العذاب is the postponed fāʿil (agent).
﴿إن في ذلك لآية﴾: giving the reason for the seizing; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿في ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and ﴿آية﴾ is the postponed noun of إن.
﴿وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, أكثرهم is its noun, and مؤمنين is its khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: Abū Jaʿfar [said]: Abū ʿUbayd related that Abū ʿAmr used to pronounce [the ṭāʾ] with fatḥa, that the Kufans pronounce it with kasra [i.e. imāla], and that the Medinans read it between fatḥa and kasra. This is explained in Sūrat «طه». The Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read «طسم» with assimilation of the nūn into the mīm — the readers say: with concealment (ikhfāʾ) of the nūn — and al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «طسين ميم» with the nūn pronounced distinctly. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to Sībawayh, the quiescent nūn and the tanwīn have four categories: they are pronounced distinctly before the guttural letters; they are assimilated before rāʾ, lām, mīm, wāw and yāʾ; they are changed into mīm before bāʾ; and they are [pronounced] from the nasal passage, i.e. not distinctly. On these four categories set out by Sībawayh, this reading is not permissible, because there is no guttural letter here such that the nūn would be pronounced distinctly according to him. But there is a justification for it, namely that the rule for the letters of the alphabet is that they are pronounced in pause, and when they are pronounced in pause the nūn is pronounced distinctly. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] related in his book «فيما يجرى وما لا يجرى» ("On what is declined and what is not") that one may say «طسين ميم» with fatḥa on the nūn and ḍamma on the mīm, just as one says هذا معدي كرب يا هذا ("this is Maʿdī Karib, O you").

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: «تِلْكَ آياتُ» is nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "these are those verses of the clear Book", i.e. those which you were promised, because they were promised in the Torah and the Gospel that the Qur'an would be sent down.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: «لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ»: [«باخع»] is the khabar (predicate) of laʿalla. «أَلَّا يَكُونُوا»: al-Farrāʾ said: it is in the position of the accusative because they [i.e. the two words] are a requital. Abū Jaʿfar said: one only says «إن» with kasra because it is a requital — that is the accepted usage. The [right] view on this is what Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said in his book «في القرآن» ("On the Qur'an"): he said: «أن» is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and the meaning is: perhaps you will kill yourself because of their abandoning faith.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: «إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ آيَةً»: a condition and its requital. «فَظَلَّتْ» means فتظلّ ("and would remain"), because the past comes with the sense of the future in requitals. We have already mentioned «خاضعين» and why He did not say خاضعات, in a way that makes any addition unnecessary.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: The root meaning of al-karam in the language is nobility and excellence; so نخلة كريمة is an excellent palm with abundant fruit, and رجل كريم is an excellent, noble, forgiving man. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-zawj is the kind (lit. "colour").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: «إِذْ» is in the position of the accusative: "and recite to them [the account of] when your Lord called Moses". What indicates this is that after it there is «وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْراهِيمَ» [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 69]. «أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ».

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: «قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ» is a badal (substitute). «أَلا يَتَّقُونَ» [with yāʾ], because they are absent from the address. «ألا تتّقون» [with tāʾ] is also permissible, in the sense of "say to them", and similar to it is «قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ» [Āl ʿImrān: 12], with tāʾ and with yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: «وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسانِي»: al-Kisāʾī said: the reading with the nominative — meaning in «وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسانِي» — has two explanations: one is a fresh start (al-ibtidāʾ), and the other is in the sense of "and I — my breast is constricted and my tongue is not loosened", i.e. coordinated with «أخاف». He said: it is also read in the accusative, and both are valid. Abū Jaʿfar said: the [right] explanation is the nominative, because the accusative is a conjunction to «يكذّبون», and this is far-fetched. What indicates this is His saying «وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي» [Ṭā Hā: 27]; this shows that this is so.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «أَنْ أَرْسِلْ» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "we have been sent so that you send the Children of Israel with us". Then Pharaoh reminded him of his favour in bringing him up.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
«قالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا وَلِيداً»: [«وليدا»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا»: if you wish, you may assimilate the thāʾ into the tāʾ because of its closeness to it. «مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ»: the ḍamma may be dropped because of its heaviness, so that one says مِن عُمْرك. Sībawayh related
fatḥa on the ʿayn with sukūn on the mīm [i.e. عَمْر], and from this comes لعمرك ("by your life"); in his view only the fatḥa is used in oaths, because of its lightness. «سِنِينَ» is a sound plural, and one may also say لبثت سنينًا يا هذا ("I stayed years, O you"), putting the case-ending on the nūn.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: The clause may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "you killed the soul while this was your state". The meaning may also be: "and you are now among those ungrateful for my favour, because you demand that I send the Children of Israel with you".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: It has been said: its meaning is "I strayed from knowing that that blow would kill".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Al-Akhfash said: it has been said that the meaning is "Or is that a favour?", with the alif of the question omitted. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not permissible, because the alif of the question produces a meaning and its omission is impossible, unless «أم» is in the sentence, in which case its omission is permissible in poetry. I know of no disagreement among the grammarians on this, except something al-Farrāʾ said: he said the omission of the alif of the question is permissible with verbs of doubt, and he related ترى زيدا منطلقا ("you see Zayd departing?") in the sense of أترى. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān used to say of such things: he took it only from the expressions of the common people; likewise in his view نعم زيدا, when [Zayd] has been mentioned before, he took only from the expressions of the common people. Al-Farrāʾ's doctrine on the meaning of «وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ» is that it is based on an omission, and that the meaning is: "By my life, it is a favour if you had done me the favour of not enslaving me, but you enslaved the Children of Israel", i.e. it only came about because you enslaved the Children of Israel. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk's view is that the meaning is: you remind me of a favour for which you have no right to remind me, i.e. this is by way of rebuke to him, and rebuke may be without a question or with a question. It may also be like «وَما أَصابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ» [al-Nisāʾ: 79], and also be a rebuke. A fourth view on both verses together is that the saying is omitted. «أن عبّدت» is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for «نعمة»; «أن» may also be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "because you enslaved the Children of Israel".

nahhas-irab:23-24.t: «قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَما رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ»: Moses ﷺ answered him, «قالَ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ», i.e. when you look at the heavens and the earth and the signs and events in them, you will know and be certain that they have a Maker and a Disposer.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
[…] upon them than the first, and closer to their understanding than the first.
So Moses ﷺ addressed the company with what was nearer. [Translator's note: the entry begins mid-sentence in the source; it is translated as it stands.]

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: So he brought a proof which they would understand from him, because they knew that they had had fathers, that these had passed away, that they must have One who causes them to pass away, that they had come into being after not having been, and that they must have One who brought them into being.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: «قالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ»: Moses ﷺ answered him on this by saying «رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ»: His dominion is not like your dominion, because you rule only one land, outside which your command does not hold, and [in which] he dies whom you do not wish to die; whereas the One who sent me rules the east and the west and what is between them. If you understand, you will see clearly what I have said.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t: «قالَ لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلهَاً غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ»: Moses ﷺ dealt gently with him and «قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ», i.e. "would you make me one of the imprisoned even if I brought you something by which the truth of what I have brought becomes clear to you?"

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: So the condition did not need an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) according to Sībawayh, because what precedes suffices for it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
«قالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: i.e. "postpone him from your [appointed] time, and postpone completing the debate with him until all the sorcerers are gathered". [One may say] أرجئه with the hamza retained in continuous speech (al-idrāj); it is permissible to drop it and keep the kasra; in continuous speech it is permissible to drop it [i.e. the vowel-letter], and to keep the ḍamma with the hamza and give the hāʾ ḍamma without a wāw.
Retaining the wāw is also permissible, though remote. It is remote only because the hamza is quiescent and the wāw is quiescent, and the barrier between them is weak. The wāw is the original and the yāʾ is a substitute for it, and both are dropped because what precedes them indicates them, and because they are both additional.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Whoever reads «أَإِنَّ لَنا لَأَجْراً» without a question makes its meaning: "you are one of those who love us and treat us kindly".

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: I.e. those who used to be called sorcerers; they are mentioned by this name to indicate that they are the ones mentioned before.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: «إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ»: deception on Pharaoh's part, and tyranny and aggression: he made out that the sorcerers had colluded with Moses, peace be upon him, in what took place, and that Moses was the one who [lit. "those who"] taught them sorcery.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «قالُوا لا ضَيْرَ», from ضار يضير. One also says ضار يضور in the sense of ضرّ يضرّ ضرّا وضررا ("to harm").

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: «أَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "because we were". Al-Farrāʾ permitted its kasra [i.e. إن], on the basis that it is a requital.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: «وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبادِي», from أسرى يسري. «أن اسرِ» is also permissible, from سرى يسري: two eloquent dialect forms.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: The lām of emphasis frequently enters the khabar (predicate) of inna, except that the Kufans do not permit إن زيدا لسوف يقوم. The proof that it is permissible is «فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ» [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 49]: this is the very lām of emphasis, entering on «سوف». «قَلِيلُونَ» is a sound plural, as one says أحدون.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: From غاظ يغيظ, and this is the eloquent dialect form.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t:
[«حذرون»] is the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr; the reading of the Kufans is «حاذِرُونَ», and it is known from ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās. «حادرون», with an undotted dāl, is the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAmmār.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning of حذرين and حاذرين is one, and this is the view of Sībawayh. He permitted هو حذر زيدا ("he is wary of Zayd"), as one says حاذر زيدا, and he recited: [al-kāmil] 312-
حذر أمورا لا تضير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
(Wary of things that do no harm, and secure against what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] related to us; he said: I heard Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī say: Abū ʿUthmān al-Lāḥiqī said: Sībawayh met me and said: "Do you know a verse in which faʿil governs the accusative?" I had nothing memorised on it, so I thought and composed this verse for him. Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī claimed that هو حذر زيدا is permissible on the basis of omitting «من». As for most of the grammarians, they distinguish between حذر and حاذر — among them al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd — and they hold that the meaning of حذر is one in whose nature wariness is, i.e. alert and vigilant; when it is like this, it is not transitive. The meaning of حاذر is "prepared", and the exegesis from the early authorities came with this. ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd said on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, «حاذِرُونَ»: he said: equipped (muʾdūn) with horses and weapons, strengthened — and this is exactly that. His word مؤدّون means they have equipment (adāt). It has been said: the meaning is "we have weapons and they have no weapons", urging [them] to fight. As for «حادرون», its meaning is derived from their saying عين حدرة, i.e. full; i.e. we are full of rage against them.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: «كَذلِكَ» is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is "the matter is thus", i.e. the matter is as We have told you of their story.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: «فَلَمَّا تَراءَا»: this is how one pauses, just as you say تجافى القوم ("the people drew apart") and تراخى إخوتك ("your brothers slackened"). You did not pause on it so as to say تجافى and تراخى. [Translator's note: this sentence is translated as printed; its point appears to be that in pause the word keeps its final alif.] Whoever pauses and says تراءى has dropped the lām [final radical] of the verb; and whoever argued that it is a verb with [the subject] placed first made an ugly mistake, because the reason in our saying تراءى is that it is like تداعى and تجافى, as we said; had [the subject] been placed after it, one would say ترآيا. If you continue, you drop [the alif] because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and say تراءى الجمعان. Al-Aʿraj and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «قالَ أَصْحابُ مُوسى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ» [i.e. لَمُدَّرَكون]. Al-Farrāʾ said: حفر and احتفر have one meaning, and likewise لمدركون and لمدّركون have one meaning. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not what the skilled grammarians say; they only say that مدركون means "overtaken", and مدّركون "one strives to overtake them", just as one says كسبت in the sense of "I obtained and gained", and اكتسبت in the sense of "I strove and sought". This is the meaning of what Sībawayh said.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: On the lightening of the second hamza, and this is the best of the ways, because they have all agreed on lightening the second when the two are in one word, as in آدم. If you wish, you may pronounce both fully and say «نبأ إبراهيم»; if you wish, you may lighten both and say «نبأ إبراهيم»; and if you wish, you may lighten the first and say «نبأ إبراهيم». [Translator's note: the variants are printed identically in the source; they differ only in how the two hamzas are pronounced.] There is a fifth way, but it is remote in Arabic — remote because it combines two hamzas as though they were in one word — and it is good in the pattern faʿʿāl because that only comes with doubling.

nahhas-irab:71-72.t:
«فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ»: [«عاكفين»] is the khabar (predicate) of «نظل».
«قالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ»: al-Akhfash said: there is an omission in it, and the meaning is: "do they hear from you?" or "do they hear your call?"; so it was omitted, as [the poet] said: [al-basīṭ] 313-
القائد الخيل منكوبا دوابرها ... قد أحكمت حكمات القدّ والأبقا
(The one who leads the horses, their hoof-backs worn, bridled with bridle-straps of leather and hemp.)
He said: al-abaq is hemp; so there is an omission, and the meaning is: "and bridle-straps of hemp were fastened". It is related from Qatāda that he read «قالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ [i.e. يُسْمِعونكم], i.e. "do they make you hear their voices?" «إِذْ تَدْعُونَ»: if you wish, you may assimilate the dhāl into the tāʾ.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: «فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي»: a singular standing for a group. Likewise one says of a woman: هي عدوّ الله and عدوّة الله ("she is an enemy of Allah"); al-Farrāʾ related both. Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about the reason for this, and he said: whoever says عدوّة, retaining the hāʾ, says it means "one who is hostile" (muʿādiya); and whoever says عدوّ for the feminine and the plural makes it in the sense of attribution (al-nasab). «إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the grammarians said it is an exception not of the same kind as the first. Abū Isḥāq permitted that it be of the same kind as the first, on the basis that they used to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and worship idols alongside Him. Al-Farrāʾ interpreted it as referring to the idols alone, the meaning in his view being: "for if I worshipped them, they would be an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds", i.e. an enemy to me on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:78-79.t:
«يَهْدِينِ» and «وَيَسْقِينِ» are without yāʾ, because omission at verse-ends is good, so that they all agree.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq, with his eminence and his standing in Arabic, read all of these with yāʾ, because the yāʾ is a noun [i.e. the pronoun] and the nūn entered only for a reason.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: Al-Ḥasan read «الذي أطمع أن يغفر لي خطاياي يوم الدين» ("my sins", plural), and he said: it is not a single sin. Abū Jaʿfar said: خطيئة in the sense of خطايا is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and they have all agreed on the singular in His saying [lit. "His strength"], Mighty and Majestic, «فَاعْتَرَفُوا بِذَنْبِهِمْ» [al-Mulk: 11], whose meaning is "their sins"; and likewise «فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ» [al-Nisāʾ: 103], whose meaning is "the prayers". So likewise «خَطِيئَتِي», if it means sins. And Allah knows best. [Translator's note: «قوّته» ("His strength") is translated as printed; «قوله» ("His saying") is evidently meant.]

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: «فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيها»: it has been said that the pronoun refers to the idols, and the report about them is in the masculine [plural] because they treated them as beings that reason. «هُمْ وَالْغاوُونَ»: those who worshipped them. «والغاوون» are those disappointed of the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: Those who called them to the worship of idols and helped Iblīs in what he wants; so they are his hosts.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: «وَما أَضَلَّنا إِلاَّ الْمُجْرِمُونَ» (99): [«المجرمون»] is nominative by its verb. «المجرمون» are those who called them to the worship of idols.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: In the position of the nominative, because the meaning is "so we have no intercessors".

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
«وَلا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ» is also permissible in the nominative, being conjoined to the position, because the meaning is "so we have no intercessors and no devoted friend". The plural of صديق is أصدقاء, صدقاء and صداق. One does not say
صُدُق, in order to distinguish the adjective from other [nouns]. The Kufans related that its plural is said to be صدقان.
This is far-fetched, because this is the plural of what is not an adjective, such as رغيف and رغفان. They also related صديق and أصادق, but afāʿil is only the plural of afʿal when it is not an adjective, such as أشجع and أشاجع. One also says
صديق for a group and for a woman. The plural of حميم is أحمّاء and أحمّة; they disliked afʿilāʾ [i.e. أحمماء] because of the doubling.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: "if a return to life were to happen to us, we would believe".

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: «كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ»: on the basis of the feminine of the collective.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: «الْأَرْذَلُونَ» is the plural of الأرذل; the broken plural is أراذل; the feminine is الرّذلى and its plural رُذَل. Dropping the alif and lām is not permissible in any of this according to any grammarian we know, and they all forbade سقطت له ثنّيتان علييان لا سفليان ("two upper front teeth, not lower ones, fell out for him") [i.e. without the article].

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: «الْفُلْكِ»: Sībawayh claimed that it is the plural of فُلْك, like أَسَد and أُسْد; and it has been said: فُلْك [singular] and فُلْك [plural] have one meaning.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: «رِيعٍ» is the plural of رِيعة.

nahhas-irab:129-129.t: So they were censured for taking what they had no need of, and rebuked by His saying «لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ», i.e. you will not live forever, so why do you build what you will die and leave behind?

nahhas-irab:137-137.t: [«خُلُق»] is the reading of Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza. Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Ḥasan read «إِنْ هذا إِلَّا خُلُقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ» with fatḥa on the khāʾ [i.e. خَلْق, "the fabrication of the ancients"]. The first reading, according to al-Farrāʾ, means "the custom of the ancients". Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad]; he said: «خلق الأولين» is their way and what their affairs ran upon. The two views are close to each other, [and close] to this hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "The most perfect of the believers in faith is the best of them in character (khuluq)", i.e. the best of them in way, custom and what their affairs run upon in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It cannot be that one of good character who is dissolute should be excellent, nor that he should be more perfect in faith than one of bad character who is not dissolute. Abū Jaʿfar said: it was related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that the meaning of «خلق الأولين» is their denial and their fabrication, except that he inclined to the first reading, because it contains their praise of their fathers, and most of what the Qur'an brings in describing them is their praise of their fathers and their saying «إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ» [al-Zukhruf: 22].

nahhas-irab:148-148.t: «وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ»: the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «نخل». The best thing said about its meaning is what al-Darāwardī related from the nephew of al-Zuhrī from his uncle, on His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ»: he said: the soft, delicate [spathe] when it first emerges; and it is the spathe in layers (al-ṭalʿ al-naḍīd), because some of it is above other parts.

nahhas-irab:149-149.t:
«وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبالِ»: one also says تنحَتون [with fatḥa], because it contains one of the guttural letters. «بيوتا فرهين» is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans; Abū Ṣāliḥ and the Kufans read «فارِهِينَ». The scholars have disagreed about the meaning of the two: some distinguished between them, and [some] made them one meaning. Abū Ṣāliḥ, Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim said: «فارهون» means skilful. Mujāhid said: «فرهون» means insolent and exultant. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a distinction between two meanings: «فارهون» would be from فره when one is skilful and energetic, and «فرهون» in the sense of فرحين ("exulting"), with the ḥāʾ replaced by hāʾ.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās «وينحتون من الجبال بيوتا فرهين»; he said: "skilful". He said: so this is in the sense of فارهين, if it is preserved correctly from Ibn ʿAbbās. Among those who held that فارهين and فرهين have one meaning are Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub. Quṭrub related: فره يفره فهو فاره, and فرع يفره فهو فره وفاره, when one is energetic. [Translator's note: «فرع» is translated as printed; «فره» (with a different vowelling) is evidently meant.] It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:155-155.t:
«قالَ هذِهِ ناقَةٌ لَها شِرْبٌ»: al-Farrāʾ said: al-shirb is the share of water. Abū Jaʿfar said:
As for the maṣdar (verbal noun), one says of it شرب شُربا, شَربا and شِربا; the most common is the one with ḍamma, because the forms with fatḥa and kasra share [their form] with something else: al-shirb is the share of water, and al-sharb is the plural of shārib ("drinker"), as [the poet] said: [al-basīṭ] 314-
فقلت للشّرب في درنا وقد ثملوا ... شيموا وكيف يشيم الشّارب الثّمل
(I said to the drinking party in Durnā, when they were drunk: "Watch [the lightning]!" — yet how can the drunken drinker watch?)
Except that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, and al-Kisāʾī choose al-sharb with fatḥa for the maṣdar, and they adduce as proof the report of some scholars that the Prophet ﷺ said: "They are days of eating and drinking (sharb)."

nahhas-irab:156-156.t: «وَلا تَمَسُّوها بِسُوءٍ»: showing the doubled letter separately is not permissible here, because they are two vowelled letters of the same kind. «فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ» is the answer to the prohibition; dropping the fāʾ from it and using the jussive is not permissible, as it is permissible with the imperative, except for something related from al-Kisāʾī, that he permits it.

nahhas-irab:157-157.t: I.e. over having hamstrung her, when they became certain of the punishment; and regret did not benefit them, because the [time of] trial had passed once certainty of the punishment had come. It has been said: regret did not benefit them because they did not repent; rather they sought out Ṣāliḥ ﷺ to kill him when they became certain of the punishment.

nahhas-irab:171-171.t: «إِلَّا عَجُوزاً» is accusative as an exception. «فِي الْغابِرِينَ»: Saʿīd related from Qatāda; he said: she remained (ghabarat) in the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, i.e. she stayed. Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is "among those who remained into old age", i.e. she lived on until she grew decrepit.

nahhas-irab:176-176.t: Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ read «أصحاب لئيكة المرسلين» [i.e. لَيْكَةَ, with fatḥa], and likewise read in [Sūrat] «صاد» [verse: 13]. The readers agreed on the genitive in the one in Sūrat «الحجر» [verse: 78] and the one in Sūrat «ق» [verse: 14], so what they disagreed on must be referred back to what they agreed on, since the meaning is one. As for what Abū ʿUbayda related, that «ليكة» is the name of the village in which they were and that الأيكة is the name of the whole land, it is something unestablished, and it is not known who said it; it was merely "said", and no proof is established by this until it is known who said it so that his knowledge may be established — and even if it were known who said it, there would be reason to examine it, because all the people of knowledge, of the exegetes and those versed in the speech of the Arabs, hold the opposite. ʿAbdallāh ibn Wahb related from Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim from Qatāda; he said: Shuʿayb ﷺ was sent to two nations: i.e. his people, the people of Madyan, and the companions of the thicket (al-ayka). He said: al-ayka is a thicket of dense trees. Saʿīd related from Qatāda; he said: the companions of the thicket were people of a thicket and trees, and most of their trees were the dawm, which is the tree of the muql [doum palm]. Juwaybir related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk; he said: the companions of the thicket went out — meaning when the heat struck them — and gathered in the thicket and the trees; then Allah sent a cloud over them, and they sought shade beneath it, and when they had all gathered beneath it, they were burnt. Even if there were nothing in this but what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās — he said: beneath it were the trees. [Translator's note: this conditional sentence is left without a main clause in the source; it is translated as it stands.] We know of no disagreement among the experts of the language that al-ayka is the dense trees. As for the argument of some who argued for the reading of those who read with fatḥa in these two places, that in the written text (al-sawād) it is «ليكة», there is no proof for him in it. The [right] view on it is that its origin is الأيكة; then the hamza was lightened, its vowel was thrown onto the lām and it dropped, and the connecting alif was dispensed with, because the lām had become vowelled. On this basis only the genitive is permissible, just as you say مررت بالأحمر ("I passed by the red one") with the hamza fully pronounced, then lighten it and say مررت بلحمر. If you wish, you write it in script as you wrote it the first time, and if you wish, you write it with the omission; and only the genitive is permissible. Likewise, in الأيكة only the genitive is permissible. Sībawayh said: know that everything that is a diptote becomes fully declined when the alif and lām enter it or it is put in construct. We know of no one who disagreed with Sībawayh on this.

nahhas-irab:184-184.t:
[«والجبلّة»] is conjoined to the kāf and the mīm. One also says «جبلّة» [with another vowelling], and the plural of both is جبال. The ḍamma and the kasra may be dropped from the bāʾ, and likewise the doubling from the lām, so that one says جبلة, جبل, جبلة and جبل. One also says
جبلة and جبال, and the hāʾ may be dropped from all of this. [Translator's note: the forms are printed without vowel marks in the source, so the different vowellings it lists cannot be distinguished here.]

nahhas-irab:192-193.t: «وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (192) نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ (193)». «نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ»: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Basra, except al-Ḥasan; he and the Kufans read «نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ» [i.e. نَزَّلَ بِهِ الرُّوحَ الأمينَ, "He sent down with it the trustworthy Spirit"]. [Translator's note: both readings are printed identically in the source.] Some experts of the language argue for this reading from His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ», because تنزيل indicates نزّل; this is a good argument, and Abū ʿUbayd mentioned it. The argument for those who read with the light form is to say: this is not the maṣdar (verbal noun) [of the verb in question], because the meaning is "and the Qur'an is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds; Gabriel ﷺ came down with it", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «قُلْ مَنْ كانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ فإنه نزّله على قلبك» [al-Baqara: 97].

nahhas-irab:196-196.t: I.e. the warning about those He destroyed is in the books of the ancients. In the reading of al-Aʿmash, «لَفِي زُبُرِ الْأَوَّلِينَ» [i.e. زُبْر]: he dropped the ḍamma because of its heaviness, as one says رُسْل.

nahhas-irab:197-197.t:
I.e. was it not [a sign] for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel who embraced Islam knew the truth of the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ? For what they have in the Torah and the Gospel is a clear sign. Whoever reads (تكن) puts it in the feminine because «أن يعلمه» is the sign, as [the poet] said: [al-kāmil] 315-
فمضى وقدّمها وكانت عادة ... منه إذا هي عرّدت إقدامها
(He went on and drove her forward — and it was his habit, whenever she shied away, to drive her forward.)
The nominative of «آية» is remote, because «أن يعلمه» is the sign. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «أن تعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل» [with tāʾ].

nahhas-irab:198-198.t: Al-Ḥasan read «على بعض الأعجميّين». Abū Jaʿfar said: one says رجل أعجم and أعجميّ when someone is not eloquent, even if he is an Arab; and رجل عجميّ is one whose origin is from the non-Arabs, even if he is eloquent, being attributed to his origin — except that al-Farrāʾ permitted saying رجل عجميّ [in the first sense].

nahhas-irab:200-201.t: Al-Farrāʾ permitted the jussive in «يؤمنون», because it carries the sense of condition and requital. He claimed, and related from the Arabs: ربطت الفرس لا ينفلت ("I tied the horse, it will not get loose"), with the nominative and the jussive; he said: because its meaning is "if I do not tie it, it will get loose". The nominative in his view is in the sense of "so that it does not get loose" and "so that they do not believe": when «كي» was omitted, it was put in the nominative. All of this talk about «يؤمنون» is a mistake according to the doctrine of the Basrans: the jussive is not permissible without something to govern it in the jussive, and nothing can exert a government stronger than that of its governor while that governor is present. This is a clear argument; and if an irregular view of some Basran deviates [from it], no attention is paid to it, since the majority disagree with him on it.

nahhas-irab:205-205.t: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: he means the people of Mecca.

nahhas-irab:206-206.t: He said: he means of the punishment and destruction.

nahhas-irab:207-207.t: The first «ما» is in the position of the accusative and the second in the position of the nominative. The first may also be a negation with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:208-209.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: «ذِكْرى» is in the position of the accusative by way of al-qaṭʿ ("detachment", i.e. as a ḥāl). This does not hold; the [right] view on it is the view of al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], that it is in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. they remind a reminding; and this is a sound view, because the meaning of «إِلَّا لَها مُنْذِرُونَ» is "except that it had reminders". The case-ending does not show in «ذكرى» because it has a shortened alif (alif maqṣūra). «ذكرى» with tanwīn is also permissible. «ذكرى» may also be in the position of the nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. "Our warning is a reminder". Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "that is a reminder" and "this is a reminder".

nahhas-irab:210-210.t: Al-Ḥasan read «الشياطون», and it is a mistake according to all the grammarians. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] say: this is how the mistake of scholars happens — it comes only through some confusion entering. When al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, saw that at its end there was a yāʾ and a nūn, while it was in a [nominative] position, it was confused for him with the sound plural, and so he made a mistake. In the hadith: "Beware of the slip of the scholar." And he himself read, with the people, «وَإِذا خَلَوْا إِلى شَياطِينِهِمْ» [al-Baqara: 14]; had this been with wāw in the nominative position, the nūn would have had to be dropped for the construct.

nahhas-irab:211-212.t: «وَما يَنْبَغِي لَهُمْ», i.e. it is not fitting for the devils to come down with the revelation and the command to obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic. «وَما يَسْتَطِيعُونَ» to fabricate the like of the Qur'an, nor to take it from the angels by stealth, because they are kept away from hearing.

nahhas-irab:213-214.t: It has been said: say this to whoever disbelieves. And it has been said: it is an address to him ﷺ, even though he would not do this, because he is protected and chosen; but he was addressed with this so that it be known [what] the judgement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, [is] concerning whoever worships other than Him, whoever he may be. After this comes what indicates it, namely «وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ», i.e. lest they rely on their lineage and their kinship with you and abandon what is obligatory on them.

nahhas-irab:215-215.t: One says خفض جناحه ("he lowered his wing") when he became gentle and kind.

nahhas-irab:216-216.t: I.e. I am innocent of your disobedience to me, because their disobeying him is their disobeying Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since he commands them only what pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and [he is innocent of] whomever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has declared Himself innocent of.

nahhas-irab:221-221.t: It has been said: the devils come down because they are mostly in the air, owing to the slightness of their constitution, and because they are like the wind.

nahhas-irab:222-222.t: I.e. a great liar who commits sin; they come down upon him, whispering disobedience to him.

nahhas-irab:223-223.t: «يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كاذِبُونَ» (223). «يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ»: it has been said: those who give ear are those upon whom they come down, i.e. they listen to the devils and accept from them. It has also been said: they are the devils, who eavesdrop by stealth.

nahhas-irab:224-224.t: The accusative is also permissible by an implied verb explained by «يتّبعهم». It has been said: «الغاوون» here are those who deviate from the truth; and this indicates that the poets too are deviators, because if they were not deviators their followers would not be so.

nahhas-irab:225-225.t: I.e. they are in the position of one wandering aimlessly, because they go in every direction of falsehood and do not follow the ways of truth; for whoever follows the truth and knows that his words are recorded against him is careful, and does not wander aimlessly, going wherever he pleases, not caring what he says.

nahhas-irab:227-227.t:
«إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ» is in the position of the accusative as an exception.
«وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا»: retaliation is only by right and within what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has set as its limit; if one goes beyond that, one has retaliated by falsehood. «وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ»: in this there is a threat to whoever retaliates wrongfully. «أيّ» is accusative by «ينقلبون», and it is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun); it may not be accusative by «سيعلم». The grammarians say: what precedes a question does not govern it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the real reason for that is that the question is one meaning and what precedes it is another meaning, so if what precedes it governed it, the meanings would enter into one another.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طسۤمۤ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: "طسۤمۤ" is a name.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾.
Because the Qurʾān is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.
So the meaning is: these are "those verses of the Book".
And it was said: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ has the meaning of "these" (هذه).

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: i.e. killing.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. killing yourself out of eagerness for them.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿بَاخِعٌ﴾ i.e. destroying.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is from بَخَعَه, i.e. he humbled him.
And the meaning is: perhaps you will kill yourself because of their abandoning faith.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ آيَةً﴾.
i.e. had We willed, We would have compelled them to obedience by destroying everyone who disobeyed.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾.
There are several statements on this:
Mujāhid said: ﴿أعناقهم﴾: their great ones (chiefs).
Abū Zayd and al-Akhfash said: ﴿أعْنَاقُهُمْ﴾: their groups; one says: جاءني عُنُقٌ من النَّاس, i.e. a group (of people) came to me.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: ﴿خَاضِعِينَ﴾ and "خاضعةً" are one and the same here.
And al-Kisāʾī holds that the meaning is: (they remained) humbled toward it [Translator's note: the source reads خاضعيها].
Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid's statement that ﴿أَعْنَاقُهُمْ﴾ are their great ones is [well known] in the language: one says جاءني عُنُقٌ من النَّاس, i.e. their chiefs; and likewise one says جاءني عُنُقٌ من الناس, i.e. a group. For this reason one says: "على فلانٍ عتْقُ رقبةٍ" (so-and-so must free a slave, lit. a neck [raqaba]), and one does not say "عَتْقُ عُنُقٍ", because of the ambiguity that occurs in it.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar's statement is the best of these statements, and it is the choice of Abū al-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad).
The meaning according to his statement is: so they remained humbled toward it. He gave the predicate about the muḍāf ilayhi, and brought the muḍāf as an inserted word (muqḥam) for emphasis, as the poet said:
رَأَتْ مَرَّ السِّنينَ أَخَذْنَ مِنّي * كَمَا أَخَذَ السِّرَارُ منَ الهِلاَلِ
(She saw the passing of the years [lit. "the passing" treated as plural] taking from me, as the last nights of the month take from the crescent.)
And as the poet said:
وتَشْرَقُ بالقَوْل الَّذي قَدْ أَذَعْتَهُ * كما شَرِقَتْ صَدْرُ القَناَةِ مِنَ الدَّمِ
(And you choke on the word that you have spread, as the head of the spear choked [feminine verb] with blood.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: And like it is: سقطتْ بعضُ أصابعه (some of his fingers fell [feminine verb]).
He said: And like it is:
يا تَيْمُ تَيْمَ عَدِيٍّ لا أَبَا لَكُمُ * لا يُلْقِيَنَّكُمُ في سَوْءَةٍ عُمَرُ
(O Taym, Taym of ʿAdī — may you have no father! — let not ʿUmar cast you into disgrace.)
So he brought the first "تَيْمَ" as inserted (muqḥam) for emphasis.
As for al-Kisāʾī's statement, it is an error according to the Basrans and al-Farrāʾ.
And such an omission does not occur anywhere in speech.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Of the plants of the earth, of what people and cattle eat.
It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī that he said: People are of the plants of the earth; whoever of them goes to Paradise is noble (karīm), and whoever goes to the Fire is base.
The meaning according to Mujāhid's statement is: of every beneficial, good kind.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً﴾.
i.e. an indication of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that there is nothing like Him.
Then He said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. Allah knew that they would not believe, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ، وَلا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
i.e. and recite this to them.
And after it: ﴿وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ. وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلاَ يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي﴾.
Al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read ﴿ويَضِيقَ صَدْرِي. وَلاَ يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with يَضِيقَ in the accusative, conjoined to يُكَذِّبُونِ].
The first reading is better, because the (non-)loosening of the tongue is not among what falls under the fear, since it had already happened.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
The meaning is: so send to Hārūn so that he may help me and support me, as you say: "Send to me, for I will help you."

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: It means the killing of the soul. ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ i.e. because of my killing a man of theirs.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿قَالَ كَلاَّ فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ﴾.
﴿كَلاَّ﴾ is a deterrent and a rebuke, i.e. desist from this fear and trust in Allah.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ﴾.
It is possible that ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ refers to Mūsā and Hārūn, peace be upon them both, because two are a plural, as He, the Exalted, said ﴿فَإنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾.
It is possible that it refers to Mūsā and Hārūn and the signs.
And it is possible that it refers to Mūsā and Hārūn and those to whom they were sent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first is the most fitting of them, so that the meaning is: We are with you, helping and strengthening.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿رسولُ﴾ has the meaning of "message" (risāla), and he recited:
لَقَدْ كَذَب الوَاشُوْنَ مَا فُهْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ * بِسِرٍّ وَلا أَرْسَلتُهم برسُوْلِ
(The slanderers have lied: I did not utter a secret in their presence, nor did I send them a message [rasūl].)
The implied form according to his statement is: we are the bearers of a message.
And al-Akhfash holds that it is a singular that indicates two and a plural.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
The meaning is: He sent us so that you send the Children of Israel with us.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً﴾.
i.e. a newborn; so he reminded him of his favour in raising him from when he was small until he grew up.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ﴾.
And (it may also be) مِن عُمْرِك and عَمْرِك.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلْتَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It means the killing of the soul.
Al-Shaʿbī read: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ﴾ with kasra on the fāʾ [i.e. فِعْلَتَك]; and fatḥa is for the first (reading), because it is for the single occurrence.
And kasra has the meaning of manner and state, i.e. your deed that is known, as he said:
كأنَّ مِشْيتَها مِنْ دَارِ جَارَتِهَا * مرُّ السَّحَابَةِ لا رَيْثٌ وَلا عَجَلُ
(As though her gait [mishya] from her neighbour's house were the passing of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)
And one says: that was in the days of al-radda and al-ridda (the apostasy).
Abū Jaʿfar said: "ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān" said — and he preferred that — since the apostasy occurred only once, fatḥa is better.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
There are several statements about its meaning:
a- Among them that the meaning is: (you are) of those ungrateful for my favour, as he said:
"والكُفْرُ مَخْبَثَةٌ لِنَفْسِ المُنْعِمِ"
(and ingratitude is a cause of disgust to the soul of the benefactor)
b- Al-Ḍaḥḥāk holds that the meaning is: and you are of the disbelievers because of your killing the Copt.
He said: So he denied disbelief of himself, and stated that he did that out of ignorance.
c- Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is: and you are now of the disbelievers.
d- Al-Suddī said: i.e. and you are of the disbelievers, because you used to follow us in the religion that you now find fault with; so you were of the disbelievers by your own statement.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the best of what has been said about its meaning is what Ibn Zayd said; he said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ — (ungrateful) for our favour, i.e. for the favour of my raising you.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿ قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذاً وَأَنَاْ مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ﴾.
i.e. of the ignorant.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ﴾ i.e. of the forgetful, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿أَنْ تَضِلَّ إحْدَاهُمَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً﴾.
Al-Suddī said: It means prophethood.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
There are several statements on this verse:
a- It was said: the interrogative alif is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is that then a favour?"
As he said:
تَرُوْحُ منَ الحَيِّ أَمْ تَبْتكِرْ * وماذا يَضُرُّك لو تَنْتَظِرْ
(Will you leave the tribe in the evening or set out at dawn? And what harm would it do you if you waited?)
But this is not permissible, because if the alif is omitted from an interrogative, the meaning disappears, unless there is "أَمْ" or something similar in the speech.
And it was said: the meaning is: "And is that a favour you remind me of, that you enslaved me while I am of the Children of Israel?"
Because it is narrated that he raised him with the intention of enslaving him.
And it was said: "And is that a favour you remind me of, that you enslaved the Children of Israel and left me (free)?"
This is the best of the statements, because the wording indicates it; i.e. this only became a favour because you took the Children of Israel as slaves; had you not taken them as slaves, it would not have been a favour. So "أَنْ" is a badal (substitute) for "نعمة".
And it may be that the meaning is: because you enslaved the Children of Israel.

nahhas-meani:23-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Mūsā ﷺ answered him by informing him of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which created beings are incapable of: ﴿قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ مُّوقِنِينَ﴾.
Pharaoh did not rebut this argument with anything more than saying: ﴿قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلاَ تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾? i.e. do you not listen to his words?
So Mūsā answered him, because he was the one intended, and gave him more explanation.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
﴿قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَآئِكُمُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾. Pharaoh did not argue against him with anything more than attributing madness to him: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِيۤ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾.
i.e. one whose mind is overcome, because he says something that he (Pharaoh) does not recognise; for Pharaoh's people held that the one they knew as their lord at that time was "Pharaoh", and that those they knew as the lords of their forefathers of old were other kings who had been before Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:28-30.t:
So Mūsā gave him more explanation and said ﴿رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Then Pharaoh threatened him: ﴿قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَـٰهَاً غَيْرِي لأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ﴾.
So Mūsā argued against him and against them with what they could witness: ﴿قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيءٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾? [verse 30].
i.e. with a decisive, clear proof that indicates my truthfulness.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
It is said: al-thuʿbān is the large serpent; and He said in another place ﴿تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ﴾.
And al-jānn is the small snake.
In this there is evidence that the sign was mighty, because He described its hugeness, and that it wriggled with the wriggling of a small one because of its lightness (agility), and its hugeness did not prevent it from that; and this is more tremendous as a sign.

nahhas-meani:33-36.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ﴾.
i.e. he drew his hand out of his bosom, and behold, it was white to the beholders, a luminous whiteness without leprosy.
Pharaoh rejected the mighty sign by attributing it to sorcery: ﴿قَالَ لِلْمَلإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
Then he humbled himself before them and said ﴿يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِّنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ؟ قَالُوۤاْ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِي ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَاشِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It means the police (al-shuraṭ).
It is narrated that the sorcerers were twelve thousand.
And that Mūsā was sent when sorcery was widespread, and he was given the mighty signs,
just as the Prophet ﷺ was sent when eloquence was at its peak, and he was given the Qurʾān, and they were challenged to produce a sūra like it, and they were unable to do that.
Qatāda said: ﴿إنَّهُ لَكَبيرُكُمْ﴾ means Mūsā ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ﴾.
It is narrated that he was the first to cut off (limbs) and to crucify.
﴿قَالُوا لاَ ضَيْرَ﴾ — in what befalls us of the punishment of this world, along with our hope for forgiveness.
One says: ضَرَرٌ, ضُرٌّ, ضَيْرٌ and ضَوْرٌ with one meaning (harm), and Abū ʿUbayda recited:
فإنَّكَ لا يَضُوْركَ بَعْدَ حَوْلٍ * أَظَبْيٌ كَانَ أمُّكَ أمْ حِمَارُ
(For it will not harm you, after a year, whether your mother was a gazelle or a donkey.)
﴿أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ المُؤْمِنينَ﴾ i.e. because we were.
Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. the first of the believers among the people of our time.
