It was said: atbaʿahu is said in the sense of ittabaʿahu with hamzat al-waṣl, that is, "he caught up with him". al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥārith al-Dhimārī read it with hamzat al-waṣl and a doubled tāʾ, and it is in the sense of "catching up".

His saying: {مُّشْرِقِينَ}: accusative as a ḥāl. The apparent sense is that it is from the agent. The meaning of mushriqīn is "entering into the time of sunrise", like aṣbaḥa and amsā, that is, entered into these two times. It was said: "entering the east", like anjada and atʾhama. And it was said: mushriqīn in the sense of "shining". In the exegesis: the Children of Israel were in light and the Copts in darkness; on this, {مُّشْرِقِينَ} would be a ḥāl from the object. In my view it may be a ḥāl from both the agent and the object, if we make mushriqīn mean "entering into the time of sunrise" or "into the place of the east", because each of the two parties was entering that time or that place.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الجمعان}: the majority read {تَرَاءَى} with the hamza fully pronounced; Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it without hamza. Its explanation is that the hamza is made light "between-between" (bayna bayna), not a pure replacement, so that three alifs do not come together: the first, the augment after the rāʾ; the second, replacing the hamza; and the third, the lām of the word; but the third does not stay in continuous reading, being omitted due to the meeting of two quiescents. Then the readers differed about the imāla of this letter, and I say: this letter is either stopped upon or not. If it is stopped upon, Ḥamza uses imāla on its last alif because it is a final one converted from yāʾ. It is necessary in its imāla that the fatḥa of the softened hamza be given imāla, because when one stops at the like of such a hamza he softens it according to his position, and he gives imāla to the first alif by following the imāla of the fatḥa of the hamza; and it is necessary in its imāla that the fatḥa of the rāʾ before it be given imāla. This is imāla for the sake of imāla.

The other readers do not use imāla on any of that, while the analogy of al-Kisāʾī's position is that he use imāla on the last alif and the fatḥa of the hamza before it. So Ibn al-Bādhish transmitted from him and from Ḥamza. If it is connected: its last alif goes because of the meeting of two quiescents, and with its going, the imāla of the fatḥa of the hamza goes, and the imāla of the augmented alif remains; and the imāla of the fatḥa of the rāʾ before it, in his view, is by taking the omitted alif into account. At that point it is said: the cause was dropped and the caused remained; since the imāla of the first alif was only because of the imāla of the last alif, as was established earlier, and the last has gone, so the first should not have imāla since what required it has gone; but he took the omitted into account and made it equal to the pronounced. That is why Abū Ḥātim assailed it and said: "Reading this letter with imāla is impossible." I said: Something resembling this procedure was given earlier in al-Anʿām at {رَأَى الْقَمَرَ} and {رَأَى الشَّمْسَ}; so look to it there.

His saying: {لَمُدْرَكُونَ}: the majority read it with sukūn on the dāl, a passive participle of adraka, that is, "overtaken". al-Aʿraj and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read it with fatḥa on the dāl, doubled, and kasra on the rāʾ. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning: following one another in perishing at their hands. Of it is the verse from al-Ḥamāsa:

3518 - أَبَعْدَ بَني أمِّي الذين تتابَعُوا ... أُرَجِّيْ الحياةَ أم مِنْ الموتِ أجْزَعُ (After the sons of my mother, who followed one another (in death), do I hope for life, or do I fear death?)

meaning: iddaraka on the pattern ifta ʿala is intransitive in the sense of 'perished and vanished'. One says iddaraka l-shayʾu yaddarikuhu, so he is muddarik, that is, perished successively; and for this reason the rāʾ has kasra." Among those who stated expressly the kasra of it is Abū l-Faḍl al-Rāzī, who said: "iddaraka on ifta ʿala may also be in the sense of afʿala, transitive; had the reading been from this, the rāʾ would have had to be fatḥa. It has not reached me from the two of them, meaning al-Aʿraj and ʿUbayd, except kasra."

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {فانفلق}: before it is an omitted clause, that is, "so he struck, and it split." Ibn ʿUṣfūr claimed that what is omitted is only "struck" and the fāʾ of "split", and that the fāʾ present is the fāʾ of "so he struck"; so he kept from each that which indicates the omitted: he kept the fāʾ of "so he struck" to point to "struck", and he kept "split" to point to the fāʾ attached to it. This is a collapsing statement.

The readers differed on making the rāʾ of {فِرْقٍ} light (tarqīq), on the authority of Warsh, because of the qāf. It was also read filq with lām in place of the rāʾ, to agree with {فَانفَلَقَ}. al-Ṭawd: the great mountain, towering in the sky.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "great"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying: {وَأَزْلَفْنَا}: that is, "We brought near to safety". {ثَمَّ} is an adverb of distant place. {الآخَرِينَ} are Mūsā and his companions. al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥaywa read {وَزَلَفْنَا}, triliteral. Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith read it with qāf, that is, azlalnā ("We made slip"). By "the others" in this reading are meant Pharaoh and his people.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: the operative in {إِذْ} is {نَبَأَ} or "Recite!" (utlu). So al-Ḥūfī said. This is possible only if {إِذْ} is a direct object. It was said: {إِذْ} is a badal of {نَبَأَ}, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). It amounts to its being governed by "Recite!" with the interpretation mentioned.

His saying: {وَقَوْمِهِ}: the hāʾ refers to Ibrāhīm, because he is the one being spoken about. It was said: it refers to his father, because he is the nearest mentioned, that is, "he said to his father and to his father's people." It is supported by {إِنِّي أَرَاكَ وَقَوْمَكَ} [al-Anʿām: 74], where he annexed the people to him.

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying: {نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَاماً}: they came in the answer with the verb stated explicitly so as to conjoin to it their saying {فَنَظَلُّ}, out of pride in it and delight in it; otherwise their saying "idols" would have been enough, like His saying the Exalted {قُلِ الْعَفْوَ} [al-Baqara: 219] and {قَالُوا خَيْراً} [al-Naḥl: 30].

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ}: there must be something omitted, that is, "do they hear your supplication", or "do they hear you supplicating?" On the first implied form, it governs one object by agreement; on the second, it governs two, with the implied clause standing in for the second. This is the position of al-Fārisī. According to others the implied clause is a ḥāl. The investigation of both views has already been given. Qatāda and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, the second object omitted, that is, "do they make you hear the answer?"

His saying: {إِذْ تَدْعُونَ}: accusative by what precedes it; what is before it and what is after it are both past in meaning, though future in expression, by the operation of the first on {إِذْ}, and the operation of {إِذْ} on the second. Some said: {إِذْ} here is in the sense of idhā. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is on the narration of a past state, and its meaning is: 'Bring to mind the [past] states in which you used to call on them, and say: did they hear you, or make you hear?' It is more effective in reproach." It has already been given that it was read with assimilation of the dhāl of idh and with its being clear before the tāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The analogy of muddakir and the like is possible in it, but no one has read it so. The analogy would be for the pronunciation to be 'iddadʿūna'; what prevented this pronunciation is the connection of the radical dāl in the verb, so the similar letters became many." I said: he means that the pronunciation would then have a doubled unpointed dāl and then a quiescent unpointed dāl.

The Shaykh said: "This is not allowable, because this replacement is only in the tāʾ of ifta ʿala after dāl, dhāl and zāy, such as iddahana, iddakara and izdajara, and after jīm irregularly, such as 'ijdamaʿū' for 'ijtamaʿū'; or in the tāʾ of the pronoun after dāl and zāy, such as 'fuzdu' for 'fuztu' and 'jaladdu' for 'jaladtu'; or the tāʾ of 'tawlaj', of which they said 'dawlaj'. The tāʾ of the imperfect is none of what he mentioned. His statement 'what prevented … ' to the end implies that it is permissible if what he mentioned were not found; and on the implication of his statement you could say, for 'idh takhruj', 'iddakhruj', and no one says that; rather they say 'ittakhruj', assimilating the dhāl into the tāʾ."

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: accusative by {يَفْعَلُونَ}, that is, "they do the like of what we do." {يَفْعَلُونَ} is accusative in position as the second object of {وَجَدْنَا}.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {عَدُوٌّ}: the higher dialect is to use ʿaduww in the singular and masculine. The Exalted said: {هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ} [al-Munāfiqūn: 4]. That was done with it only by likening it to verbal nouns such as al-walūʿ and al-qabūl. It may also be said aʿdāʾ and ʿaduwwa. His saying {عَدُوٌّ لِي} is on its original form, with no implied muḍāf and no inversion. It was said: idols do not show enmity, being inanimate, so the implied form is "their worshippers are an enemy to me." And it was said: rather there is an inversion in the speech, its implied form being "I am an enemy to them." These two are the weaker, because the speech is sound without them.

His saying: {إِلاَّ رَبَّ العالمين}: there are two views on it. One: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), that is, "but the Lord of the Worlds is not an enemy to me." al-Jurjānī said: "There is fronting and delaying in it, that is: 'Do you see what you worshipped, you and your ancient forefathers — except the Lord of the Worlds — for they are an enemy to me', with illā meaning 'other than' (dūna) and 'besides' (siwā)." The second: that it is connected. This is the position of al-Zajjāj, because they used to worship Allah the Exalted and the idols.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "meaning" in al-Jurjānī's statement; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَنِي}: there are several views on it: accusative as an adjective of {رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ}, or a badal, or ʿaṭf bayān, or by the implied "I mean"; and nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the One who created me", or as a mubtadaʾ.

His saying: {فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ}: a nominal clause, nominative in position as its khabar. al-Ḥūfī said: "The fāʾ entered because of what the mubtadaʾ includes of the sense of the condition." This is rejected, because the relative is specific, not general, and because the ṣila cannot have renewal in it, so it does not resemble the condition. Abū l-Baqāʾ followed al-Ḥūfī but did not address the fāʾ. If he meant what al-Ḥūfī meant, then what is in it has been given; and if he did not mean it, he follows al-Akhfash in allowing the redundant fāʾ in the khabar absolutely, such as "Zaydun fa-ḍribhu", and its investigation has already been given.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying: {وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي}: it may be a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, and likewise what follows it. It may be that these are attributes of {الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي}. The entry of the wāw is permissible; its investigation has been given at the beginning of al-Baqara, as in:

3519 - إلى المَلِكِ القَرْمِ وابنِ الهُمامِ ... وليثِ الكتيبةِ في المُزْدَحَمْ (To the king, the chief, and son of the noble one, and lion of the battalion in the throng)

Ibn Abī Isḥāq retained the yāʾ of the first-person speaker in {يَسْقِينِ}, {يَشْفِينِ} and {يُحْيِينِ}, and this is also related from ʿĀṣim. The majority read {خَطِيئَتِي} in the singular. al-Ḥasan read khaṭāyāya, a broken plural.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {مِن وَرَثَةِ}: it is either a second object, that is, "settled" or "being among the heirs", or an adjective of an omitted element which is the second object, that is, "an heir from among the heirs".

semin-durr:88-88.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ يَنفَعُ}: a badal of {يَوْمَ} before it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made this part of the speech of Allah the Exalted up to the end of the verses, while parsing {يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ} as a badal of {يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ}. The Shaykh rejected it, because the operative in the badal is the operative in the one substituted for, or another like it implied; and on both views it is not sound, because of the difference of speakers.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَتَى الله}: there are several views on it. First: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), that is, "but whoever comes to Allah with a sound heart, that will benefit him." al-Zamakhsharī said: "In addition to that you must imply a muḍāf, namely the state, by which soundness is meant, and it is not of the genus of wealth and children, so that the meaning would come to: wealth and children do not benefit, only soundness of heart benefits; and had the muḍāf not been implied, the exception would not have gained a meaning."

The Shaykh said: "There is no necessity calling for omitting the muḍāf as he mentioned." I said: He implied the muḍāf only so that it would be imagined that the excepted is included in that from which the exception is made, for unless that is imagined, the exception does not occur; that is why they forbade "the horses neighed except the camels" unless by interpretation.

Second: that it is a direct object of {لَا يَنفَعُ}, that is, "wealth and children do not benefit except this person, for it benefits him: his wealth spent in the ways of righteousness, and his righteous sons, because he taught them and was good to them." Third: that it is a badal from the omitted object, or from that from which the exception is made, since the implied form is: "neither wealth nor children benefit anyone of the people except one with this description." The one excepted from is omitted, as in his saying:

3520 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولم يَنْجُ إلاَّ جَفْنَ سيفٍ ومِئْزرا (… and he escaped with nothing but a sword sheath and a waist-wrapper)

that is, "he did not escape with anything". Fourth: that it is a badal of the agent of {يَنفَعُ}, so it is nominative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He gave precedence to the rational, so the implied form is: 'except the wealth of whoever', or 'the sons of whoever', for he benefits himself and others by intercession."

I said: Abū l-Baqāʾ mixed one view with another: when we wish to make it a badal of the agent of {يَنفَعُ}, we have two ways. One: the way of precedence (taghlīb), i.e. we give the sons precedence over the wealth, and the exception is made from the sons, as though it were said: "the sons do not benefit except the son who comes with a sound heart, for he benefits himself by his righteousness and others by intercession." The second way: that you imply an omitted muḍāf before {مَنْ}, that is, "except the wealth of whoever" or "the sons of whoever"; so the views become five.

al-Zamakhsharī justified the connected sense of the exception in two ways. One: "except the state of whoever comes to Allah with a sound heart," and this is from his saying:

3521 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعُ (… their greeting to one another is a painful blow)

"and its reward is only the sword", and an example is that it be said: "Does Zayd have wealth and children?" and it is answered: "His wealth and sons are the soundness of his heart." You mean the negation of wealth and children from him and the affirmation of soundness of his heart in place of that. The second: he said: "If you wish, you may carry the speech by meaning and make wealth and children in the sense of riches, as though it were said: 'on a day when no wealth benefits except the wealth of the one who comes', because a man's wealth in his religion is the soundness of his heart, as his wealth in his worldly life is his money and his sons."

semin-durr:91-91.t: His saying: {وَبُرِّزَتِ}: Mālik ibn Dīnār read {وَبَرَزَتْ} with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a light rāʾ, active, ascribed to {الْجَحِيمُ}, which is why it is nominative.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying: {فَكُبْكِبُواْ}: that is, they were thrown and overturned one upon another. al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-Kabkaba is the repetition of al-kabb. He made the repetition in the expression an indication of repetition in the meaning." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something similar, saying: "This is the correct view, because the repetition of the verb is evident, as in ṣarra and ṣarṣara." This is the position of al-Zajjāj. In the like of this pattern there are three positions. One: this one. The second, the position of the Basrans: that all the letters are radical. The third, the position of the Kufans: that the third is a replacement for a letter like the second, so the original of kabkaba is kabbaba with three bāʾs; similarly lamlama and kafkafa. This is when the meaning remains sound with the dropping of the third; but if the meaning is not sound with its dropping, all are radical without disagreement, such as simsim and khimkhim.

The wāw of {كُبْكِبُوا}: it was said to refer to the idols, treating them as rational beings; and it was said: to their worshippers.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "one"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:96-96.t: His saying: {وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya) parenthetical between the saying and what it governs; what it governs is the oath clause.

semin-durr:97-97.t: His saying: {إِن كُنَّا لَفِي}: the position of the Basrans is that {إِنْ} is the lightened form and the lām is the distinguishing lām; the position of the Kufans is that {إِنْ} is negative and the lām is in the sense of illā.

semin-durr:98-98.t: His saying: {إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ}: {إِذْ} is accusative, either by {مُبِينٍ} or by an omitted element, that is, "we were astray at the time of our equating you with Allah in worship." It may, though weakly, be governed by {ضَلَالٍ}, and the meaning is according to it. But its weakness is a technical one: that a described maṣdar does not operate after its description.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying: {حَمِيمٍ}: al-ḥamīm is the near, from their saying "ḥāmmatu fulān", that is, his intimates. al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-Ḥamīm is from ihtimām (concern), and it is from the concern; or from al-ḥāmma, which is the intimate circle; and it is the sincere friend." The negation here may be a negation of the friend altogether, or of his attribute only, so it belongs to the chapter of:

3522 - على لاحِبٍ لا يهتدى بمنارِه ... (On a clear road not guided by its signposts …)

al-Ṣadīq may be singular, and may be used for the plural, as ʿaduww is used for it; one says hum ṣadīq and hum ʿaduww.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {فَلَوْ أَنَّ}: it may be the one imbued with the meaning of wishing (tamannī), in which case it has no apodosis according to the well-known view, and the accusative of {فَنَكُونَ} is the answer to the wish which {لَوْ} conveys. It may be on its regular footing, its apodosis omitted, that is, "we would have found intercessors and friends" or "we would have done righteousness." On this the accusative of the verb is by an implied {أَنْ} conjoined to {كَرَّةً}, that is, "if we had a return, and so we would be", like her saying:

3523 - لَلُبْسُ عَباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عيني ... (Wearing a cloak, and my eye being cooled …)

semin-durr:105-105.t: His saying: {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ}: he made the verb of qawm feminine only because it is feminine, by the evidence of its diminutive quwayma. It was said: because it is in the sense of "community" (umma). And since its individual members are rational, male and female, the pronoun returns to it by giving precedence to the masculine, so it was said {لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ}. The object of {تَتَّقُونَ} is omitted, that is, "do you not fear Allah's punishment?"

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying: {وَاتَّبَعَكَ الأَرْذَلُونَ}: a circumstantial clause, from the kāf of {لَكَ}. ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥaywa read {وَأَتْبَاعُكَ} nominative, the plural of tābiʿ like ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb, or of tabīʿ like sharīf and ashrāf, or of tabaʿ like baram and abrām. In its being nominative there are two views. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ and {الأَرْذَلُونَ} its khabar; the clause is also circumstantial. The second: that it is conjoined to the nominative pronoun in {نُؤْمِنُ}, and the separation by the preposition made that good; and {الأَرْذَلُونَ} is its adjective.

The Yemeni read {وَأَتْبَاعِكَ} genitive, conjoined to the kāf in {لَكَ}. That is weak, or forbidden according to the Basrans. On this, {الأَرْذَلُونَ} is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are the lowliest." The root of al-arthal has already been given in Hūd.

semin-durr:112-112.t: His saying: {وَمَا عِلْمِي}: {مَا} admits two views. One, which is the apparent sense: that it is interrogative, nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, with {عِلْمِي} its khabar, and the bāʾ attached to it. The second: that it is negative, with the bāʾ also attached to {عِلْمِي}. So al-Ḥūfī said, and it needs an implied khabar so that the speech becomes a clause with it.

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying: {لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted, and the object of {تَشْعُرُونَ} too.

al-Aʿraj and Abū Zurʿa read {لَوْ يَشْعُرُونَ} with the yāʾ of the third person, which is an iltifāt (shift of person). It is not good for it to refer back to the believers.

semin-durr:118-118.t:
His saying: {فَتْحاً}: it may be a direct object, in the sense of "that which is opened", and may be a confirmatory maṣdar.

His saying: {وَنَجِّنِي}: that from which one is saved is omitted because the meaning is understood, that is, "from what will befall my people." {مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ} is a clarification (bayān) of His saying {مَنْ مَعِي}.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "opened"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:119-119.t: His saying: {الْمَشْحُونِ}: that is, filled, loaded. One says: shaḥanahā ʿalayhim khaylan wa-rijālan ("he filled it against them with horses and men"). al-Shaḥnāʾ: enmity, because it fills the chests with rancour. al-Fulk here is singular, by the evidence of its being described with a singular; the discussion of it has already been given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying: {تَعْبَثُونَ}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of {تَبْنُونَ}. al-Rīʿ, with kasra or fatḥa on the rāʾ, is the plural of rīʿa. In the language it is the elevated place. Dhū l-Rumma said:

3524 - طِراقُ الخَوافي مُشْرِفٌ فوقَ رِيْعَةٍ ... ندى ليلِه في رِيْشه يَتَرَقْرَقُ (Layer upon layer of feathers beneath, looking out over a high place, the dew of its night glistening on its feathers)

Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the road," and recited for al-Musayyab ibn ʿAlas, describing women's litters:

3525 - في الآلِ يَخْفِضُها ويَرْفَعُهما ... رِيْعٌ يَلُوْحُ كأنه سَحْلُ (In the mirage, a rīʿ lowers them and raises them, gleaming as though it were a saḥl)

The commentators differed in expressing it, with many views. al-Rayʿ, with fatḥa: what accrues of tribute (kharāj).

ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ (١٩٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِلِسَانٍ): the bāʾ may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) الْمُنْذِرِينَ, and it may be a badal (substitute) from «بِهِ», i.e. "he brought it down in a clear Arabic tongue", that is, with a message, or a language.

ukberi-tibyan:197-197.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةً أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (١٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ): it is read with tāʾ (تكن), and in it there are two views. The first: it is the complete (tāmma) [kāna], the fāʿil (agent) is «آيَةٌ», and «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a badal (substitute), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); i.e. "has there not come about for them a sign?" The second: it is the deficient (nāqiṣa) [kāna], and concerning its noun there are two views. One of them: it is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «آيَةً» is a fronted khabar, and the clause is the khabar of kāna. The second: its noun is «آيَةٌ», and concerning the khabar there are two views. One of them: [the khabar is] «لَهُمْ», and «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a badal, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
The second: [the khabar is] «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ».
It is permissible for the khabar to be definite here because the indefiniteness and definiteness of the maṣdar (verbal noun) are the same, and «آيَةً» has been specified by «لَهُمْ», and because no particular [instance] is intended by the knowledge of the Children of Israel.
It is also read with yāʾ (يكن); so it may be like [the reading with] tāʾ, because the feminine gender is not real.
And with yāʾ it has also been read with آيَةً in the accusative (naṣb), on the basis that it is a fronted khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:198-198.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَاهُ عَلَى بَعْضِ الْأَعْجَمِينَ (١٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْأَعْجَمِينَ): i.e. الْأَعْجَمِيِّينَ, the yāʾ of relation (yāʾ al-nisba) having been omitted, just as they said الْأَشْعَرُونَ, meaning الْأَشْعَرِيُّونَ. Its singular is أَعْجَمِيٌّ. It cannot be the plural of أَعْجَمُ, because its feminine is عَجْمَاءُ, and a word like this is not given the sound plural.

ukberi-tibyan:200-200.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ سَلَكْنَاهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (٢٠٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَلَكْنَاهُ): its like has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Ḥijr. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:202-203.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٢٠٢) فَيَقُولُوا هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنْظَرُونَ (٢٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ), (فَيَقُولُوا): both are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «يَرَوْا».

ukberi-tibyan:207-207.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يُمَتَّعُونَ (٢٠٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ): it may be an interrogative, in which case «مَا» is in the position of the accusative; and it may be a negation, i.e. "it did not avail them anything."

ukberi-tibyan:209-209.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذِكْرَى وَمَا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ (٢٠٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذِكْرَى): it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the warning is a reminder."

ukberi-tibyan:223-223.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَاذِبُونَ (٢٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُلْقُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «تَنَزَّلُ».

ukberi-tibyan:225-225.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ (٢٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَهِيمُونَ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ», and so it governs «فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), in which case the khabar is «فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ».
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ (٢٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ): it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and its operator is «يَنْقَلِبُونَ», i.e. "they will turn with a turning, whatever turning [it be]." «يُعْلَمُ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has سَيَعْلَمُ.] does not govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t: Allah the Exalted says: (طسم (١) تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (٢) لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ (٣)). (طسم): like الم, and it was mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara. (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ): like ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابُ. And (أَنْ لَا يَكُونُوا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "so that not" (لِئَلَّا), or "for fear that not" (مَخَافَةَ أَنْ لَا).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَظَلَّتْ), i.e. "and then would remain" (فَتَظَلُّ); its position is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). It may also be nominative, as resumptive.
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَاضِعِينَ): it is put in the masculine plural for four reasons. The first: what is meant by الأعناق ("the necks") is their great men. The second: He meant the owners of their necks. The third: it is the plural of عُنُق in the sense of a group of people, so it means the groups, not the necks. The fourth: since He annexed الأعناق to a masculine [rational] noun, and they are joined to them in their physical make-up, He applied to them the rule that applies to their owners.
Al-Kisāʾī said: «خَاضِعِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) belonging to the genitive pronoun, not to الأعناق. On close examination this is far-fetched, because «خَاضِعِينَ» would then be predicated of something other than the agent of ظلّت, so it would require the agent pronoun to be made overt; it would have had to be: خَاضِعِينَ هُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمْ): in the position of the accusative, governed by «أَنْبَتْنَا». And «مِنْ كُلِّ» is a tamyīz (specification); it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ نَادَى رَبُّكَ مُوسَى أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ نَادَى), i.e. "and mention when He called" (وَاذْكُرْ إِذْ نَادَى). And (أَنِ ائْتِ): أنْ is maṣdar-forming, or in the sense of أي ("that is", explicative).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْمَ): it is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it.
(أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ): it is read with yāʾ, as resumptive, and with tāʾ, as direct address; the implied wording [on the latter] is: "O people of Pharaoh" (يَا قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ). It is also said that it [قوم] is the object of يتقون.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلَا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَى هَارُونَ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي): in the nominative, as resumptive, i.e. "and I – my breast is constricted by the denial"; and in the accusative, conjoined to the accusative verb before it. Likewise (يَنْطَلِقُ).
(فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَى هَارُونَ), i.e. "an angel to inform him that he is my support", or "a prophet with me".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ): there are several views on its being singular. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الرسالة ("the message"), i.e. "bearers of a message" (ذَوَا رَسُولٍ), or "we are a message", by way of hyperbole. The second: it makes do with one of the two, since they were both on one mission. The third: Moses, peace be upon him, was the principal and Aaron a follower, so He mentioned the principal.

ukberi-tibyan:18-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ (١٨) وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ عُمُرِكَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سِنِينَ».
And (فَعْلَتَكَ) is with fatḥa; it has also been read with kasra, i.e. "[the manner of doing] customary with you".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتِلْكَ): the interrogative particle is omitted, i.e. "and is that…?" (أَوَتِلْكَ).
And (تَمُنُّهَا) is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of نعمة; the preposition is omitted, i.e. "with which [you reproach me]" (بِهَا). It is also said: «عَلَيَّ» is construed with ذِكْر or with عَبْد. [Translator's note: so in the source («حُمِلَ عَلَيَّ بِذِكْرٍ أَوْ بِعَبْدٍ»); the intended sense is unclear, and it may be corrupt.]
And (أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ) is a badal (substitute) of نعمة; or it is on the implied "it is" (هِيَ); or a badal of the hāʾ in تمنّها; or in the position of the genitive with the bāʾ implied, i.e. "in that you enslaved" (بِأَنْ عَبَّدْتَ).

ukberi-tibyan:23-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢٣) قَالَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ): he used «مَا» only because he was asking about His attributes and acts, i.e. "what are His attributes and what are His acts?" Had he meant His essence, he would have said مَن ("who"); for that reason Moses, peace be upon him, answered him with his words: «رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ».
It is also said: he was ignorant of what the question really was, so Moses brought the real answer.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لِلْمَلَأِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ): [حوله is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الملأ, i.e. "being around him".
The Kufans said: the qualified noun is omitted, i.e. "those who were around him" (الَّذِينَ حَوْلَهُ). There are many questions here which were mentioned in al-Aʿrāf and Ṭā Hā.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَلْقَوْا حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغَالِبُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ), i.e. "we swear" (نَحْلِفُ).

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَايَانَا أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ كُنَّا), i.e. "because we were" (لِأَنْ كُنَّا).

ukberi-tibyan:54-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ (٥٤) وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَائِظُونَ (٥٥) وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ (٥٦))
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَلِيلُونَ): put in the plural according to the meaning, because الشرذمة ("the band") is a group.
And (حَذِرُونَ), without alif, and with alif, are two dialectal forms. It is also said: الحاذر, with alif, is the one who is armed. It is also read with dāl [حَادِرُونَ]; الحادر is the strong one, and also the one filled with rage or fear.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ), i.e. "a bringing out like that" (إِخْرَاجًا كَذَلِكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُشْرِقِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). المُشرِق is the one upon whom sunrise has come.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمُدْرَكُونَ), without doubling and with doubling; one says أَدْرَكْتُهُ and ادَّرَكْتُهُ ("I overtook him").

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَزْلَفْنَا): with fāʾ, i.e. "We brought near"; the reference is to the companions of Moses.
It is also read, irregularly (shādhdh), with qāf [وَأَزْلَقْنَا], i.e. "We brought the people of Pharaoh to a slippery place".

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ): what governs إذ is «نَبَأَ» [Translator's note: the source has «نَبَّأَ»; the word in the preceding verse is نَبَأَ, "the story".].

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ (٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and on the mīm, i.e. "do they hear your calling?" (يَسْمَعُونَ دُعَاءَكُمْ); the muḍāf was omitted because «تَدْعُونَ» indicates it.
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, i.e. "do they make you hear the answer to your calling upon them?"

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا كَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): accusative, governed by «يَفْعَلُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي): it is put in the singular as denoting a relation (ʿalā al-nasab), i.e. "people of enmity"; for that reason one says of a feminine: هِيَ عَدُوٌّ, just as one says حائض ("menstruating", without the feminine ending); but عَدُوَّةٌ has also been heard.
(إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is an exception from a different genus (disjunctive), because He is not included in the number [of the enemies]. The second: it is from the same genus, because among their forefathers there were those who worshipped Allah and others besides Allah. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي): «الَّذِي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «فَهُوَ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «يَهْدِينِي» its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of «الَّذِي».
As for the occurrences of «الَّذِي» after it, they are adjectives of the first الذي; the wāw may be brought in between adjectives. It is also said that what is conjoined is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, being dispensed with by the khabar of the first.

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ (٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ), i.e. "an heir from among the heirs of…" (وَارِثًا مِنْ وَرَثَةِ…); so من is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:87-89.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ (٨٧) يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ (٨٨) إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ): it is a badal (substitute) of the first «يَوْمَ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is from a different genus (disjunctive), i.e. "but whoever comes to Allah… will be safe" or "will benefit".
The second: it is connected (muttaṣil); and in this there are two views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative, as a badal of the omitted [object], or as an exception from it; the implied wording is: "neither wealth nor sons will benefit anyone, except whoever comes…" (لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ أَحَدًا إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى). The meaning is that when wealth is spent in the ways of righteousness, and [in the case of] righteous sons, the one connected to them and to their righteousness benefits from them. The second view: it is in the position of the nominative as a badal of the agent of ينفع, the rational being given precedence; the implied wording is then: "except the wealth of whoever…" or "the sons of whoever…", for that benefits himself or others through intercession.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: it may be the object of ينفع, i.e. "that benefits no one except a man who comes to Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ): what governs it may be «مُبِينٌ», or an omitted verb indicated by «ضَلَالٌ»; ضلال cannot govern it, because it has been qualified by an adjective.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٠٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَنَكُونَ): it is conjoined to «كَرَّةً», i.e. "if only we could return and be", that is, "and that we be" (فَأَنْ نَكُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاتَّبَعَكَ): the wāw is circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl).
It has been read irregularly (shādhdh) «وَأَتْبَاعُكَ» ("and your followers"), as a plural; there are two views on it:
The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is the khabar (predicate), the clause being a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The second: it is conjoined to the agent pronoun in «نُؤْمِنُ», and (الْأَرْذَلُونَ) is an adjective, i.e. "are we and they to be equal?"

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتْحًا): it may be an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), الفتح then meaning "what is opened (judged)", as they said: "this is among the conquests (فتوح) of ʿUmar".

ukberi-tibyan:128-129.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ (١٢٨) وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ (١٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَعْبَثُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تَبْنُونَ».
And (تَخْلُدُونَ) is read in the active voice without doubling, and in the passive both with doubling and without it; the past is خلد and أخلد.

ukberi-tibyan:132-133.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي أَمَدَّكُمْ بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٣٢) أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ وَبَنِينَ (١٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ): this clause is explicative of what precedes it, and it has no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:136-137.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ (١٣٦) إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا خُلُقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٣٧))
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ): this clause stands in the place of "or did not admonish" (أَمْ لَمْ تَعِظْ).
(إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا خُلُقُ): with fatḥa on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [خَلْقُ], i.e. "the fabrication of the ancients", that is, like their fabrication.
It may also mean the people [created], i.e. "are we and you anything but like those who came before, in claiming messengership and in denial, and we die and are not brought back?"
It is also read with two ḍammas [خُلُقُ], i.e. "the custom of the ancients".

ukberi-tibyan:146-147.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَتْرُكُونَ فِي مَا هَاهُنَا آمِنِينَ (١٤٦) فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي جَنَّاتٍ): it is a badal (substitute) of His saying «هَاهُنَا», with the preposition repeated.

ukberi-tibyan:149-149.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَارِهِينَ (١٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِهِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also read «فَارِهِينَ» with alif; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ (١٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْقَالِينَ), i.e. "surely one who detests, among those who detest" (لَقَالٍ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ); so «مِنَ» is an adjective of the khabar (predicate), attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, and the lām [of لعملكم] is attached to the omitted khabar. In this way one escapes placing the ṣila before the relative [i.e. the dependent of the definite participle before it], since if you made «مِنَ الْقَالِينَ» the khabar, you would make it govern «لِعَمَلِكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (١٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ): it is read with kasra on the tāʾ, with the hamza pronounced fully, and with it lightened by transferring [its vowel to the lām], like الأنثى and الُانثى.
It has also been read «لَيْكَةَ», with a yāʾ after the lām and fatḥa on the tāʾ. This is not sound, since there is no word «لَيْكَةُ» in the language that could be made a proper name; and if it is claimed that the hamza was changed into a lām, that is extremely far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:184-184.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالْجِبِلَّةَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْجِبِلَّةَ): it is read with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ, and with ḍamma on them, with doubling [of the lām]; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:192-193.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٩٢) نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ (١٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the Qurʾān, though it has not been mentioned.
And التنزيل is in the sense of "what is sent down" (المُنزَل).
(نَزَلَ بِهِ): it is read in the active voice, the agent being «الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ», and in the passive with doubling.
It is also read in the active voice with doubling, with «الرُّوحَ» in the accusative, i.e. "Allah sent down Gabriel with the Qurʾān"; and «بِهِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿طسم﴾ — it was read with the nūn assimilated (idghām) into the mīm and the letters joined to one another; and it was read "طَسِينْ مِيمْ", pronouncing the nūn distinctly and pausing on the nūn. It is also permissible — though I know of no one who read it so — to say "طَسِمِيمًا", making "طسم" a name for the sura, in the manner of his saying "خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ" (fifteen); but reciting it so is not permitted.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ — there are two ways (wajhān) in it. One of them is on the meaning that they had been promised the Quran on the tongue of Moses, so the meaning would be: "these are the verses of the Book which you were promised on the tongue of Moses"; and (the other is) on the meaning: "these are the verses of the clear Book". We have explained that at the beginning of Sūrat "al-Baqara", in His saying: ﴿الم﴾ [al-Baqara: 1] ﴿ذَلِكَ الكِتابُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 2].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ ألا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — Abū ʿUbayda said: its meaning is "destroying yourself"; and it was said: "killing yourself". This is like His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ عَلى آثارِهِمْ إنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أسَفًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]. The position of "أنْ" is accusative, as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "perhaps you are killing yourself because of their abandoning faith". So Allah, Glorified is He, informed him that had He wished to send down what would compel them to obedience, He would have been able to do so; but He, Mighty and Majestic, has laid upon them worship by which, together with faith, they merit reward, and He sent down for them signs by which the truth becomes clear to whoever seeks it. As for if punishment were sent down upon everyone who turns obstinately from the truth at the time of his obstinacy, he would submit under compulsion and believe with the faith of one who finds no way of escape from faith.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ﴾ — its meaning is "then their necks would remain (fa-taẓallu)", because in the apodosis (jazāʾ) the past-tense form occurs with a future meaning. You say "إنْ تَأْتِنِي أكْرَمْتُكَ", meaning "أُكْرِمْكَ" (I will honour you); and "إنْ أتَيْتَنِي وأحْسَنْتَ", meaning "and you do good and act well". He said "خاضِعِينَ" while mentioning the necks, because the meaning of the submission of the necks is the submission of the owners of the necks; since submission is only by the submitting of the necks, it is permissible to make the statement about the muḍāf ilayhi, as the poet said:
رَأتْ مَرَّ السِّنِينَ أخَذْنَ مِنِّي ∗∗∗ كَما أخَذَ السِّرارُ مِنَ الهِلالِ
(She saw the passing of the years — they took from me as the dark of the month takes from the crescent.)
Since years exist only by passing, he made the statement about the years, even though he had annexed the passing to them. Similar to that also is the saying of the poet:
مَشَيْنَ كَما اهْتَزَّتْ رِماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ∗∗∗ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked swaying as lances sway whose tips the passing of the gentle breezes has set tossing.)
as though he said "the winds set them tossing" (tasaffahathā, feminine), since winds exist only by passing. It came in the exegesis that by "أعْناقُهم" their great ones and their chiefs are meant; and it came in the language that "أعْناقُهم" means their groups: one says "جاءَ لِي عُنُقٌ مِنَ النّاسِ", that is: a group. Some of them mentioned another way; they said: "فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ هم", with "هم" implied, and recited:
تَرى أرْباقَهم مُتَقَلِّدِيها كَما ∗∗∗ صَدِئَ الحَدِيدُ عَنِ الكُماةِ
(You see their halters — wearing them round their necks — as iron grows rusty on armoured warriors.)
This is not permissible in the Quran. It is, on the basis of the badal of error (badal al-ghalaṭ), permissible in poetry, as though he said: "he sees their halters, he sees those wearing them", as though he said: "he sees a people wearing their halters". Had it been on the omission of "هم", it would also have been among what is permissible in poetry.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أنْباءُ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾: "أنْباءُ" means reports. The meaning is: "they will come to know the news of that at the Resurrection"; and it is possible that some of that is hastened for them in this world, such as what befell them on the Day of "Badr".

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى الأرْضِ كَمْ أنْبَتْنا فِيها مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾: the meaning of "زَوْجٍ" is: kind; and the meaning of "كَرِيمٍ" is: praiseworthy in what is needed, with the meaning of "of every beneficial kind", the causing of which to grow and the bringing of which into being none is able to do except the Lord of the worlds.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
Then He said: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآيَةً﴾: an indication that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is One, and that created things are signs pointing to the Creator being One; there is nothing like Him.
His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ أكْثَرُهم مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ means: most of them were not going to believe, that is: Allah knew that most of them would never believe, as He said: ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 3], that is: you are not worshipping what I worship now; ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 5], in what is to come; and like His saying in the story of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36], so He informed him that most of them would not believe.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذْ نادى رَبُّكَ مُوسى أنِ ائْتِ القَوْمَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative, on the meaning: "and recite this story among what you recite". The proof of that is His saying, conjoined to this story: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 69].

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي ولا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسانِي﴾ — with the accusative and the nominative. Whoever reads the nominative conjoins it to "أخافَ", on the meaning: "I fear, and my breast is constricted"; and whoever reads the accusative conjoins it to "أنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ وأنْ يَضِيقَ صَدْرِي وألّا يَنْطَلِقَ لِسانِي". The nominative is more common in recitation. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ إلى هارُونَ﴾, that is: "so that he may help me and support me in my affair"; this was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَهم عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ فَأخافُ أنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾: by the "sin" he means the man whom he struck with his fist and killed: I fear that they will kill me for my killing him.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿قالَ كَلا فاذْهَبا بِآياتِنا﴾: "كَلّا" is a deterrent and a rebuke against persisting in this supposition, as though He said: desist from this supposition and trust in Allah.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَقُولا إنّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ means: "we are the message of the Lord of the worlds", that is: "bearers of the message of the Lord of the worlds". The poet said:
لَقَدْ كَذَّبَ الواشُونَ ما بُحْتُ عِنْدَهم ∗∗∗ بِسِرٍّ ولا أرْسَلْتُهم بِرَسُولِ
(The slanderers have lied: I disclosed no secret to them, nor did I send them with any message.)

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿أنْ أرْسِلْ مَعَنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾: the position of "أنْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "we have been sent so that you send", that is: "so that you send the Children of Israel with us".

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿قالَ ألَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا ولِيدًا﴾, that is: as a newborn, when you were born. ﴿وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا مِن عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ﴾ — "مِن عُمْرِكَ" with the mīm quiescent is permissible, and "مِن عَمْرِكَ" with fatḥa on the ʿayn is permissible. One says "العُمْرُ", "اَلْعُمُرُ" and "اَلْعَمْرُ" for a person's lifetime; but in an oath nothing is permissible except "لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ", nothing else, with fatḥa on the ʿayn. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans mentioned that (the word in) the oath has fatḥa and nothing else. So Pharaoh reckoned it against Moses that he had raised him as a child from the time he was born until he grew up.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ﴾ — al-Shaʿbī read "فِعْلَتَكَ" with kasra on the fāʾ; the fatḥa is better and more common, because he means: "you killed the person, your (single) killing", on the pattern of the single instance. Al-Shaʿbī read it with the meaning: "and you killed in the manner of killing that you know", because he killed him with a single blow of the fist. One says "جَلَسْتُ جَلْسَةً" meaning "one time", and "جَلَسْتُ جِلْسَةً" with kasra meaning the manner of sitting. ﴿وَأنْتَ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ﴾ — there are two ways in it. One of them: "of those ungrateful for my favour"; the other: "and you are of the disbelievers by your killing the one you killed". So Moses ﷺ denied disbelief and admitted that this deed of his had been ignorance, and said: ﴿قالَ فَعَلْتُها إذًا وأنا مِنَ الضّالِّينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 20], that is: of the ignorant. It has been read: "وَأنا مِنَ الجاهِلِينَ".

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْمًا﴾: the Torah is meant, in which is the judgement of Allah.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ أنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾ — the exegetes took it as a denial that this could be a favour, as though he said: "so what favour do you have over me in your having enslaved the Children of Israel?!". The wording is the wording of a statement (khabar), and the meaning can be taken as they said, given that its wording is that of a statement; and in it there is a rebuke to the one addressed, as though he said to him: "this is a favour — that you took the Children of Israel as slaves!", by way of rebuking Pharaoh. The wording requires that Moses ﷺ said: "this is a favour because you took the Children of Israel as slaves and did not take me as a slave". One says "عَبَّدْتُ الرَّجُلَ" and "أعْبَدْتُهُ": I took him as a slave. The position of "أنْ" is nominative as a badal (substitute) for "نِعْمَةٌ", as though he said: "and that is a favour: your enslaving the Children of Israel and your leaving me not a slave". It is also possible for "أنْ" to be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being: "it only became a favour to me because you enslaved the Children of Israel", that is: "had you not done what you did, my family would have looked after me and would not have cast me into the river; so it only became a favour through the affliction you inflicted". The poet said, on "أعْبَدْتُ" meaning "I took as a slave":
عَلامَ يُعْبِدُنِي قَوْمِي وقَدْ كَثُرَتْ ∗∗∗ فِيهِمْ أباعِرُ ما شاؤُوا وعِبْدانُ؟
(Why do my people take me as a slave, when among them camels and slaves have multiplied, as many as they please?)

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وما رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — Moses ﷺ answered him with that which is an indication of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, through what He created, the like of which created beings are unable to produce. He said: ﴿رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 24]. Pharaoh was perplexed and gave no answer back by which to refute this statement, so he said to those around him: ﴿ألا تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 25]. Moses increased him in clarity and said: ﴿رَبُّكم ورَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 26]. He did not answer him this time either, but said: ﴿إنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إلَيْكم لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 27]. Then Moses said, in further clarification: ﴿قالَ رَبُّ المَشْرِقِ والمَغْرِبِ وما بَيْنَهُما إنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 28]. In none of these things did he answer him with a refutation of his argument.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿قالَ لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إلَهًا غَيْرِي لأجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ المَسْجُونِينَ﴾ — so he increased him in clarity and argued with what he and the assembly around him witnessed: ﴿قالَ أوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 30] ﴿قالَ فَأْتِ بِهِ إنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 31] ﴿فَألْقى عَصاهُ فَإذا هي ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 32]. The thuʿbān is the large kind of snake.
If someone says: how then does it come: ﴿فَإذا هي ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 32], while in another place: ﴿تَهْتَزُّ كَأنَّها جانٌّ﴾ [al-Naml: 10], and the jānn is the small kind of snake? The answer: this is among what indicates the greatness of the sign; that is, its form was the form of the thuʿbān, while its quivering, its motion and its nimbleness were like the quivering and nimbleness of the jānn.

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿وَنَـزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإذا هي بَيْضاءُ لِلنّاظِرِينَ﴾: he drew his hand from the opening of his garment and brought it out white with a luminous whiteness, without harm (sūʾ), that is: without leprosy. He (Pharaoh) had no way of repelling what he witnessed except to say: this is sorcery: ﴿قالَ لِلْمَلإ حَوْلَهُ إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 34]; so he made the miraculous sign sorcery.

zajjaj:35-35.t: Then he humbled himself and submitted to those who were among his followers, and said: ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكم مِن أرْضِكم بِسِحْرِهِ فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾ ﴿قالُوا أرْجِهْ وأخاهُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 36] — with kasra on the hāʾ and with ḍamma, and with the yāʾ and the wāw: "أرْجِهِي" and "أرْجِهُو وأخاهُ". ﴿وابْعَثْ في المَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 36]. The meaning of "أرْجِهْ" is: postpone him; and it came in the exegesis: detain him and his brother; the meaning is one. Its interpretation is: postpone him from this present time of yours, and postpone completing the debate with him until the sorcerers are gathered for you.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ — this made it unnecessary to say: "so he sent and gathered the sorcerers".

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ نَعَمْ وإنَّكم إذًا لَمِنَ المُقَرَّبِينَ﴾, that is: you will have, along with your wage and your reward for overcoming Moses if you overcome him, in addition to that benefit, nearness and closeness with me. It is read "أئِنَّ لَنا لَأجْرًا" as a question; and "إنَّ لَنا لَأجْرًا" is permissible, not as a question but out of their confidence in him: they said "we shall surely have a reward", that is: you are one who gives us gifts and rewards us.

zajjaj:44-44.t: ﴿فَألْقَوْا حِبالَهم وعِصِيَّهم وقالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إنّا لَنَحْنُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ ﴿فَألْقى مُوسى عَصاهُ فَإذا هي تَلْقَفُ ما يَأْفِكُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 45], that is: of what they had gathered of their stratagem and their staffs. It is related of them that they were twelve thousand sorcerers. So Moses, peace be upon him, was given victory at a time when sorcery was at its greatest and most dominant over the people of that age; and his sign was a dazzling sign in two respects: one of them, that he brought what created beings are incapable of; and the second, that the sorcerers, numbering this many, were thrown down in prostration.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿قالُوا آمَنّا بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — so they surrendered the matter to Allah, and what cannot be repelled became clear to them. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ was sent when the Arabs were at their most poetic, their most eloquent in oratory and their most articulate; and he called them to faith in Allah with the signs which the Prophet ﷺ brought and with the Quran, by which he challenged them to produce a sura like it, and they were unable to produce a sura like it. It is also related that the sorcerers were nineteen thousand.
His saying: ﴿فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 49]: the lām has entered upon "سَوْفَ" with the meaning of tawkīd (emphasis). The Kufans did not permit "إنَّ زَيْدًا لَسَوْفَ يَقُومُ", yet the entry of the lām upon سَوْفَ has occurred, and that is because the lām is emphatic.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أيْدِيَكم وأرْجُلَكم مِن خِلافٍ﴾ — it is related in the exegesis that the first to cut off (hands and feet) and to crucify was Pharaoh.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿قالُوا لا ضَيْرَ إنّا إلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾, that is: there is no harm to us in what befalls us in this world, along with our hope of forgiveness.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا نَطْمَعُ أنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنا رَبُّنا خَطايانا أنْ كُنّا أوَّلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — with fatḥa on "أنْ", that is: because we were the first of the believers. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that they were the first believers among the people of their age; but I do not think he knew the report in the exegesis, because it came in the exegesis that those who were with Moses, peace be upon him, were six hundred thousand, and it was said: six hundred and seventy thousand. Rather, the meaning of ﴿أنْ كُنّا أوَّلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is: the first to believe in this situation, upon the appearance of Moses's sign, when they had thrown down their ropes and their staffs and had exerted themselves in their sorcery. One says "لا ضَيْرَ" and "لا ضَوْرَ" with the meaning of "لا ضُرَّ" and "لا ضَرَرَ" (no harm).

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَأوْحَيْنا إلى مُوسى أنْ أسْرِ بِعِبادِي﴾: one says "أسْرى، يُسْرِي" when one travels by night; and "سَرى يَسْرِي" — it was said that it too has the meaning of "أسْرى، يُسْرِي".

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ في المَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ﴾, that is: he sent those who would gather the army for him; its meaning is: "so he gathered his host". Then he said: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 54]. "اَلشِّرْذِمَةُ" in the speech of the Arabs is: a small number. It is related that those whom he called a "شِرْذِمَة" were six hundred and seventy thousand, while Pharaoh's vanguard was seven hundred thousand, every man of them on a stallion with a helmet on his head; so he reckoned those with Moses, peace be upon him, as few in view of the great size of his own host. He said "قَلِيلُونَ", putting "قَلِيلًا" in the plural, just as one says "هَؤُلاءِ واحِدُونَ", putting واحِد in the plural, as al-Kumayt said:
فَقَدْ رَجَعُوا كَحَيٍّ واحِدِينا
(So they returned like a single tribe, as ones.)

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهم لَنا لَغائِظُونَ﴾: one says "قَدْ غاظَنِي فُلانٌ" (so-and-so has enraged me); whoever says "أغاظَنِي" has committed a solecism (laḥn).

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنّا لَجَمِيعٌ حاذِرُونَ﴾ — it is also read "حَذِرُونَ". It came in the exegesis that the meaning of "حاذِرُونَ" is muʾdūn, that is: possessing equipment (adāt), that is: possessing weapons, and weapons are the equipment of war. So "اَلْحاذِرُ" is the one prepared, and "اَلْحَذِرُ" is the one alert.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأتْبَعُوهم مُشْرِقِينَ﴾, that is: at the time of sunrise. One says "أشْرَقْنا", that is: we entered upon the time of the rising of the sun. One says "شَرِقَتِ الشَّمْسُ" when it rises, and "أشْرَقَتْ" when it shines and becomes clear; and "أشْرَقْنا نَحْنُ": we entered upon sunrise.

zajjaj:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا تَراءى الجَمْعانِ﴾, that is: when the host of Moses stood facing the host of Pharaoh — the companions of Moses had gone out by night — the companions of Moses said: ﴿إنّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ﴾, that is: the host of Pharaoh, this great multitude, will overtake us, and we have no strength against them.

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿قالَ كَلا إنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ﴾, that is: Moses said "كَلّا", that is: desist and be restrained, for they will not overtake us.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأوْحَيْنا إلى مُوسى أنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصاكَ البَحْرَ فانْفَلَقَ فَكانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ﴾, that is: every part that separated from it, ﴿كالطَّوْدِ العَظِيمِ﴾, that is: like the great mountain.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَأزْلَفْنا ثَمَّ الآخَرِينَ﴾, that is: We brought the others near to drowning there, and they are the companions of Pharaoh. Abū ʿUbayda said: (it means) We gathered the others there; he said: and from that "مُزْدَلِفَةُ" was called "جَمْعًا" (Jamʿ). Both statements are good and fine, because gathering them is bringing them near to one another. The origin of "اَلزُّلْفى" in the speech of the Arabs is: nearness.

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ means: the report of Abraham.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ﴾ means: persisting in worshipping them.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكم إذْ تَدْعُونَ﴾ — if you wish, you pronounce the dhāl distinctly, and if you wish, you assimilate it into the tāʾ, making it a tāʾ, and say "إتَّدْعُونَ"; this is better in Arabic because of the closeness of the dhāl to the tāʾ. "إذَّدْعُونَ" is also permissible, but it was not read so, just as he said "مُدَّكِرْ", whose origin is "مُذْتَكِرْ".

zajjaj:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — the grammarians said: it is an exception not from (the kind of) the first, that is: "but the Lord of the worlds". It is also possible that they worshipped idols and other things along with Allah, so he said to them: everything you worship is an enemy to me except the Lord of the worlds, because they had made their gods equal to Allah; so he informed them that he had dissociated himself from what they worshipped except Allah, for he did not dissociate himself from worshipping Him.

zajjaj:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِي أطْمَعُ أنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that his sin was his saying: "Sarah is my sister".
And his saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا فاسْألُوهُمْ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63], and his saying: ﴿فَقالَ إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 89]. We have explained the meaning of his saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63]. The meaning of "خَطِيئَتِي" is that the prophets are human beings, and error may befall them; except that they — the blessings of Allah be upon them — do not commit major sins, because they are protected (maʿṣūmūn), chosen over the worlds; every prophet is superior to all the people of his age.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لِي لِسانَ صِدْقٍ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ means: grant me good praise that remains until the end of time.

zajjaj:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ الجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ means: "it was brought near"; its interpretation is the nearness of their entering it and their looking at it.

zajjaj:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ الجَحِيمُ لِلْغاوِينَ﴾, that is: it was made manifest to those astray; "اَلْغاوِي" is the one astray.

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيها﴾, that is: in Hell. The meaning of "كُبْكِبُوا" is: they were thrown on top of one another. The lexicographers said: its meaning is: they were tumbled down (duhwirū). Its reality in the language is the repetition of falling headlong, as though when he is thrown he falls on his face time after time until he settles in it — he seeks refuge with Allah from it.

zajjaj:97-97.t: His saying: ﴿تاللَّهِ إنْ كُنّا لَفي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ ﴿إذْ نُسَوِّيكم بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 98] means: by Allah, we were in nothing but manifest error when we made you equal to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that we exalted you and worshipped you as Allah is worshipped.

zajjaj:105-105.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ — the tāʾ (of the feminine) has entered although the people of Noah are masculine, because the meaning is: "the community of the people of Noah denied". He said "اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ", while it is possible that they denied Noah alone; but whoever denies one messenger of Allah's messengers has denied the whole group and opposed it, because every messenger commands belief in all the messengers. It is also possible that it is "they denied all the messengers".

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ لَهم أخُوهم نُوحٌ ألا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ — "أخُوهم" was said because he was from among them; and every messenger comes in the language of his people, so as to make the proof clear to them and to be clearer for them.

zajjaj:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿قالُوا أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ — it is also read "وَأتْباعُكَ الأرْذَلُونَ", and in Arabic it is good and strong, because the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial) accompanies nouns more often in Arabic: you say "جِئْتُكَ وأصْحابُكَ الزَّيْدُونَ"; "وَصَحِبَكَ الزَّيْدُونَ" is also permissible, but more common is "جِئْتُكَ وقَدْ صَحِبَكَ الزَّيْدُونَ". It was said concerning His saying ﴿الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ that they attributed them to weaving and cupping; but crafts do no harm in matters of religion.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿مِنَ المَرْجُومِينَ﴾, that is: with stones.

zajjaj:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿فافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَهم فَتْحًا﴾ means: "judge between me and them with a judgement"; and the judge is called "اَلْفَتّاحُ" from this.

zajjaj:119-119.t: His saying: ﴿فِي الفُلْكِ المَشْحُونِ﴾: its singular is "فَلَكٌ" and its plural is "فُلْكٌ". Sībawayh claimed that it is in the manner of "أسَدٌ" and "أُسْدٌ", and that the analogy of "فُعْلٌ" is the analogy of "فَعَلٌ". Do you not see that you say "قُفْلٌ" and "أقْفالٌ", "جُمْلٌ" and "أجْمالٌ", and likewise "أسَدٌ", "أُسْدٌ" and "آسادٌ", and "فُلْكٌ", "فَلَكٌ" and "أفْلاكٌ" in the plural? "اَلْمَشْحُونُ" is the filled; one says "شَحَنْتُهُ", that is: I filled it.

zajjaj:128-128.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ﴾ — it is read "رِيعٍ" and "رَيْعٍ", with kasra on the rāʾ and with fatḥa. In the language it is the elevated place of the land; and from that is "كَمْ رَيْعُ أرْضِكَ؟", that is: "how high is your land?". It came in the exegesis: "بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ" means every fajj, and "اَلْفَجُّ" is the road opening through a mountain; and it also came: "on every road". His saying "آيَةً" means: a landmark.

zajjaj:129-129.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصانِعَ لَعَلَّكم تَخْلُدُونَ﴾: the singular of "اَلْمَصانِعُ" is "مَصْنَعَةٌ" and "مَصْنَعٌ", and they are what are made for water (cisterns); and it was said: buildings. The meaning of "لَعَلَّكم تَخْلُدُونَ" is: so that you may live forever, that is: and you take buildings for living forever, not reflecting on death.

zajjaj:130-130.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا بَطَشْتُمْ بَطَشْتُمْ جَبّارِينَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that their assault was with the whip and the sword. He only censured them for that because it was injustice; as for (assault) in the right, assault with the whip and the sword is permissible.

zajjaj:137-137.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا خُلُقُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — it is also read "خَلْقُ الأوَّلِينَ". Whoever read "خُلُقُ الأوَّلِينَ" with ḍamma on the khāʾ, its meaning is: the custom of the ancients; and whoever read "خَلْقُ" with fatḥa on the khāʾ, its meaning is: their fabrication and their lying. In "خَلْقُ الأوَّلِينَ" there is another way, that is: "we have been created as those before us were created; we live as they lived and die as they died, and we will not be resurrected", because they denied the resurrection.

zajjaj:148-148.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ﴾: "اَلْهَضِيمُ" is that which is pressed into itself; and it is — according to what was said — that its fresh dates are without stones. It was also said: "اَلْهَضِيمُ" is that which crumbles readily. "اَلْهَضِيمُ" in the language is the slender, pressed into itself, and there is nothing in a spathe more excellent than this.

zajjaj:149-149.t: His saying "فَرِهِينَ" — it came in the exegesis: "insolent"; and it came in the exegesis: "exultant". It was also read ﴿فارِهِينَ﴾, and the meaning of "فارِهِينَ" is: skilful. "فَرِهِينَ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:153-153.t: His saying: ﴿مِنَ المُسَحَّرِينَ﴾, that is: of those who have a saḥr, and "اَلسَّحْرُ" is the lung; that is: you are only a human being like us. It is also possible that "مِنَ المُسَحَّرِينَ" is of the pattern "اَلْمُفَعَّلِينَ" from "اَلسِّحْرُ" (sorcery), that is: of those who have been bewitched time after time.

zajjaj:166-166.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ ما خَلَقَ لَكم رَبُّكم مِن أزْواجِكُمْ﴾ — Ibn Masʿūd read: "ما أصْلَحَ لَكم رَبُّكم مِن أزْواجِكم". By it the private parts are meant, and the exegesis is on that basis. That is because the people of Lot used to turn away, with women, from the private parts to the backsides; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that by this deed of theirs they were transgressors (ʿādūn), and "عادُونَ" means: wrongdoers to the utmost degree of wrongdoing. It is related that Ibn ʿUmar was asked about taḥmīḍ and said: "Do Muslims do that?!". Taḥmīḍ is the deed of the people of Lot with women and men; and whoever permits this with women is gravely mistaken.

zajjaj:168-168.t:
﴿قالَ إنِّي لِعَمَلِكم مِنَ القالِينَ﴾: "اَلْقالِي" is the one who abandons a thing, hating it with the utmost hatred.
His saying: ﴿إلا عَجُوزًا في الغابِرِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 171] — it came in the exegesis: "among those who remained in the punishment". "اَلْغابِرُ" in the language is the one remaining; and they recited, from al-ʿAjjāj:
فَما ونى مُحَمَّدٌ مُذْ أنْ غَفَرْ ∗∗∗ لَهُ الإلَهُ ما مَضى وما غَبَرْ
(Muhammad has not slackened since God forgave him what had passed and what remained.)
And they recited, from al-ʿAjjāj:
لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأغْبارِها ∗∗∗ إنَّكَ لا تَدْرِي مَنِ النّاتِجُ
(Do not leave the last of the milk in the udders of the dry she-camels; you do not know who will deliver their young.)
[Translator's note: this second verse is usually attributed to al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza, not al-ʿAjjāj; the attribution is translated as written.]
"أغْبارُها" is what remains of the milk in the teats of the she-camel.

zajjaj:176-176.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَّبَ أصْحابُ الأيْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾: "اَلْأيْكَةُ" is dense, intertwined trees. One says "أيْكَةٌ" and "أيْكٌ", like "أجْمَةٌ" and "أجْمٌ", the distinction between its singular and its plural being the hāʾ. It is said in the exegesis that these Companions of the Thicket were people of dense, intertwined trees; and it is said that their trees were the dawm, and the dawm is the doum palm (muql). Most of the readers keep the alif and lām in "اَلْأيْكَةِ"; Abū ʿAmr and most of the readers read it so. The people of Medina read "أصْحابُ لَيْكَةِ" with fatḥa on the lām, and when one pauses on "أصْحابُ" he says "لَيْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ" [Translator's note: as written; with the Medinan reading the final vowel would be fatḥa]. It is likewise without alif in the codex (muṣḥaf) in this sura, and likewise also in Sūrat "Ṣād", without alif, while in the rest of the Quran it is with alif. It is permissible — and it is very good — to say "كَذَّبَ أصْحابُ لايْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ", without alif in the writing, with kasra, on the basis that the origin is "اَلْأيْكَةِ" and the hamza has been dropped, so that it was said "لَيْكَةَ". The Arabs say "اَلْأحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", and when they drop the hamza they say "اَلَحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", with fatḥa on the lām and keeping the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl); and they also say "لاحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", meaning "اَلْأحْمَرُ". The retention of the alif and lām in both of them in the rest of the Quran indicates that the omission from it of the hamza, which is the connecting alif, is in the manner of their saying "لاحْمَرُ". Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself] said: I mean that reading "لَيْكَةِ" in the genitive, intending "اَلْأيْكَةِ" with the lām, is better than making it "لَيْكَةِ" without supposing the alif and lām and giving it fatḥa because it is a diptote — because "لَيْكَةَ" is not known; it is only "أيْكَةٌ" for the singular and "أيْكٌ" for the plural. So the best reading in it is the kasra with the dropping of the hamza, in agreement with the codex. The people of Medina read the fatḥa according to what came in the exegesis that the name of the city belonging to those to whom Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, was sent was "لَيْكَةُ". Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām used to prefer the reading of the people of Medina, and the fatḥa, because "لَيْكَةَ" is a diptote; and he mentioned that he preferred that because it agrees with the written text, together with what came in the exegesis — as though the city is called "اَلْأيْكَةَ" and the thicket that contains these trees is called "اَلْأيْكَةَ". The kasra is good, as we have described, and I believe it has indeed been read so.

zajjaj:184-184.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والجِبِلَّةَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ is conjoined to the kāf and mīm; the meaning is: "fear Him who created you and created the earlier generations (al-jibilla)". It is also read "والجُبُلَّةَ" with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ; and "والجِبْلَةَ الأوَّلِينَ" and "والجُبْلَةَ الأوَّلِينَ" are permissible. As for the first two, they are read; and these two are permissible.

zajjaj:187-187.t: His saying: ﴿فَأسْقِطْ عَلَيْنا كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ — and "كِسْفًا"; both are read. Whoever read "كِسْفًا" with the sīn quiescent, its meaning is: "a portion"; and whoever read "كِسَفًا", its interpretation is: "pieces from the sky", the plural of "كِسْفَةٌ" — "كِسَفٌ", like "كِسْرَةٌ" and "كِسَرٌ".

zajjaj:189-189.t: His saying: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأخَذَهم عَذابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ﴾: "اَلظُّلَّةُ" was a cloud that overshadowed them, so they gathered beneath it seeking refuge in it from the heat that had afflicted them that day; then it closed in upon them, and it was among the days of greatest punishment in this world. ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — had it been outside the Quran, "عَظِيمًا" would have been permissible; but the genitive is better, as the Quran has it.

zajjaj:193-193.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿نَـزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأمِينُ﴾ ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194] — it is also read "نَزَّلَ بِهِ الرُّوحَ الأمِينَ", the meaning being: "Allah sent down with it the Trustworthy Spirit". "اَلرُّوحُ الأمِينُ" is Gabriel, peace be upon him.
His saying: ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194] means: he descended upon you and your heart retained it and it became firm, so you will never forget it nor anything of it, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 6].

zajjaj:196-196.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَفي زُبُرِ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — its interpretation, and Allah knows best, is that the mention of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the mention of the Quran are in the scriptures of the ancients. "اَلزُّبُرُ" are the books: "زَبُورٌ" and "زُبُرٌ", like your saying "رَسُولٌ" and "رُسُلٌ"; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهم في التَّوْراةِ والإنْجِيلِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 157].

zajjaj:197-197.t:
